attributes.references: Climate FieldView; DTN Data Transmission Network; John Deere Operations Center; IoT sensor standards

attributes.name: dew_point_c
attributes.description: Dew point temperature in degrees Celsius, representing the temperature at which air becomes saturated with moisture. Used for frost risk prediction, fungal disease pressure modeling (e.g., gray mold, downy mildew), and spray window determination under IPM frameworks.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; IPM disease pressure models; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: et_mm
attributes.description: Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) calculated for the observation interval using the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith method, in millimeters. SSOT for irrigation scheduling, water balance modeling, and crop water use estimation. Integrates with Climate FieldView and Granular Farm Management irrigation modules.
attributes.references: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET method; USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView; Granular Farm Management

attributes.name: frost_alert
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this observation triggered a frost or freeze alert condition (temperature at or below 0°C). Drives automated notifications for frost protection actions (e.g., wind machine activation, irrigation frost protection), crop insurance event documentation, and PHI compliance tracking.
attributes.references: USDA RMA crop insurance frost event documentation; GLOBALG.A.P.; Climate FieldView alert framework

attributes.name: gdd_base10_c
attributes.description: Growing Degree Day (GDD) accumulation for the observation interval using a base temperature of 10°C, calculated as max(0, (temp_max_c + temp_min_c)/2 - 10). Used for crop phenology tracking, pest emergence prediction, and harvest timing optimization. Standard base for corn and many broadacre crops.
attributes.references: USDA crop GDD standards; Climate FieldView GDD models; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: interval
attributes.description: Configured measurement interval for this observation record. Determines the temporal resolution of the time-series data. Supported intervals: 5-minute, 15-minute, hourly, and daily aggregations. Drives GDD and ET calculation granularity.
attributes.references: Climate FieldView; DTN weather feed standards; WMO No. 8

attributes.name: leaf_wetness_hours
attributes.description: Duration of leaf surface wetness during the observation interval, in hours. Critical input for fungal and bacterial disease pressure models under IPM frameworks (e.g., fire blight, late blight, botrytis). Drives spray timing recommendations and PHI (Pre-Harvest Interval) compliance tracking.
attributes.references: IPM (Integrated Pest Management) disease models; GLOBALG.A.P.; EPA PHI compliance

attributes.name: observation_status
attributes.description: Quality lifecycle status of the observation record. Raw records are ingested as-is; validated records have passed QC checks; flagged records have anomalies under review; corrected records have been adjusted; rejected records are excluded from downstream calculations.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8 Quality Control procedures; FSMA data integrity requirements; ISO 22000

attributes.name: observation_type
attributes.description: Classifies whether the record represents an instantaneous point reading, an interval average, a daily summary aggregation, or a forecast value ingested from DTN or WASDE feeds. Drives downstream processing logic for GDD and ET calculations.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; DTN Data Transmission Network standards; WASDE reporting framework

attributes.name: observed_at
attributes.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the meteorological measurement was captured at the sensor or station. This is the principal real-world event time used for time-series analysis, GDD accumulation, ET computation, and crop insurance documentation. Stored in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; WMO No. 8 Guide to Meteorological Instruments; FSMA traceability requirements

attributes.name: precipitation_mm
attributes.description: Total liquid precipitation (rainfall) accumulated during the observation interval, in millimeters. Core input for irrigation scheduling, water balance calculations, crop insurance loss documentation, and FSMA water quality compliance tracking.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; USDA NRCS; FSMA Produce Safety Rule; crop insurance MPCI standards

attributes.name: qc_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes from the automated QC process or manual data reviewer describing the reason for a suspect, fail, or estimated quality flag. Supports audit trail requirements for crop insurance documentation and FSMA traceability.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; FSMA traceability requirements; USDA RMA crop insurance audit standards

attributes.name: quality_flag
attributes.description: WMO-aligned quality control flag for the observation record. Pass = all values within expected range; Suspect = one or more values outside climatological bounds but not definitively erroneous; Fail = confirmed erroneous values; Missing = one or more required measurements absent; Estimated = gap-filled using interpolation or neighboring station data.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8 Quality Control; USDA NRCS data quality standards; ISO 22000 data integrity

attributes.name: relative_humidity_pct
attributes.description: Relative humidity as a percentage (0–100%) measured during the observation interval. Critical input for spray window determination (REI compliance), fungal disease pressure modeling under IPM frameworks, and ET calculation via the Penman-Monteith method.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; FAO-56 Penman-Monteith; EPA REI (Restricted Entry Interval) compliance; IPM standards

attributes.name: sensor_depth_cm
attributes.description: Depth below the soil surface at which soil temperature and soil moisture readings were captured, in centimeters. Required for multi-depth sensor arrays to correctly attribute readings to the appropriate soil horizon. Null for atmospheric measurements.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS soil monitoring standards; IoT sensor installation specifications

attributes.name: sensor_height_m
attributes.description: Height above ground level at which atmospheric measurements (temperature, humidity, wind) were captured, in meters. Standard WMO height is 2m for temperature/humidity and 10m for wind. Required for ET calculation height corrections and data quality validation.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8 instrument siting standards; FAO-56 Penman-Monteith height correction

attributes.name: snowfall_mm
attributes.description: Snowfall accumulation during the observation interval expressed as millimeters of water equivalent. Used for spring soil moisture forecasting, field access planning, and crop insurance documentation in winter crop regions.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; USDA NRCS; MPCI crop insurance standards

attributes.name: soil_moisture_pct
attributes.description: Volumetric soil moisture content as a percentage of field capacity, measured at the sensor depth. Core input for irrigation scheduling decisions, drought stress monitoring, and VRA (Variable Rate Application) prescription generation. Integrates with John Deere Operations Center and Trimble Ag Software.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; FAO irrigation scheduling guidelines; VRA standards; John Deere Operations Center

attributes.name: soil_temperature_c
attributes.description: Soil temperature measured at the sensor depth during the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Used for planting window determination (germination threshold monitoring), soil microbial activity modeling, and fertilizer application timing optimization.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; Trimble Ag Software; Climate FieldView; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: solar_radiation_wm2
attributes.description: Incoming solar radiation (shortwave) measured during the observation interval, in watts per square meter (W/m²). Primary driver of ET (Evapotranspiration) calculations via the Penman-Monteith method and NDVI-based crop growth modeling. Also used for solar energy resource assessment on farm.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; FAO-56 Penman-Monteith; NDVI calculation standards; USDA NRCS

attributes.name: source_record_code
attributes.description: Original record identifier from the upstream source system (e.g., DTN feed message ID, Climate FieldView observation UUID, John Deere Operations Center telemetry record ID). Enables end-to-end data lineage tracing from raw ingestion to Silver Layer.
attributes.references: DTN Data Transmission Network; Climate FieldView; John Deere Operations Center; FSMA data lineage requirements

attributes.name: spray_window_open
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether current meteorological conditions (wind speed, temperature, relative humidity, precipitation) meet the criteria for a safe and compliant pesticide or fertilizer application window. Derived from EPA label requirements and IPM BMP thresholds. Supports REI and PHI compliance.
attributes.references: EPA pesticide application label requirements; IPM BMP standards; GLOBALG.A.P.; FSMA

attributes.name: temperature_avg_c
attributes.description: Mean air temperature for the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Computed as (max + min) / 2 for daily intervals or as a true average for sub-daily intervals. Primary input for ET (Evapotranspiration) calculations and irrigation scheduling models.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET method; USDA NRCS

attributes.name: temperature_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum air temperature recorded during the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Used for GDD (Growing Degree Day) accumulation calculations, heat stress threshold monitoring, and crop insurance documentation. Paired with temperature_min_c for daily range analysis.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; USDA NRCS; GDD calculation standards; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: temperature_min_c
attributes.description: Minimum air temperature recorded during the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Critical for frost/freeze alert generation, GDD base temperature calculations, chilling hour accumulation, and crop protection decision support.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; USDA NRCS; GDD calculation standards; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when this observation record was last modified in the Silver Layer, such as after QC correction, status change, or data enrichment. Supports audit trail and change data capture (CDC) for downstream consumers.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; FSMA data integrity requirements; SOX audit trail standards

attributes.name: wind_direction_deg
attributes.description: Prevailing wind direction during the observation interval, expressed in meteorological degrees (0–360°, where 0/360 = North). Used for spray drift modeling, pesticide application compliance, and field-level wind exposure analysis.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; EPA pesticide application label requirements; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: wind_gust_ms
attributes.description: Maximum instantaneous wind gust speed recorded during the observation interval, in meters per second. Used for equipment safety alerts, spray application go/no-go decisions, and crop lodging risk assessment.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; EPA pesticide application label requirements; OSHA field safety standards

attributes.name: wind_speed_ms
attributes.description: Average wind speed during the observation interval, in meters per second. Used for spray window determination (drift risk assessment), ET calculation, and wind damage risk alerts. EPA pesticide label compliance requires wind speed checks before application.
attributes.references: WMO No. 8; EPA pesticide application label requirements; FAO-56 Penman-Monteith; GLOBALG.A.P.

products.name: forecast
products.description: Meteorological forecast record sourced from DTN, NOAA NWS, or Climate FieldView for a specific geographic location or field polygon. Captures forecast horizon (hourly, daily, 7-day, seasonal), predicted temperature range, precipitation probability and amount, wind speed/direction, humidity, ET forecast, and confidence interval. Supports planting window decisions, spray window scheduling, and WASDE-aligned seasonal outlooks.
products.reference: DTN Weather Forecast Feed / NOAA NWS

attributes.name: forecast_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each meteorological forecast record in the agricultural weather domain.
attributes.references: Internal Data Architecture Standard

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: Reference to the agricultural field polygon for which this forecast is generated, enabling field-level planting window and spray window decisions. Sourced from Esri ArcGIS field mapping or Climate FieldView.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS; Climate FieldView; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor from which this forecast is anchored or associated. Links to the weather station master record.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS Station Network; DTN Weather Services

attributes.name: cloud_cover_pct
attributes.description: Forecast percentage of sky covered by clouds for the valid period. Influences solar radiation estimates used in ET evapotranspiration calculations and NDVI Normalized Difference Vegetation Index interpretation.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; FAO Penman-Monteith

attributes.name: confidence_interval_pct
attributes.description: Quantitative confidence interval expressed as a percentage (e.g., 90 for a 90% confidence interval) associated with the forecast values. Supports probabilistic risk assessment for crop insurance documentation and WASDE-aligned seasonal outlooks.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS Ensemble Forecast Products; WASDE (USDA); DTN Weather Services

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: Qualitative confidence level assigned by the forecast provider indicating the reliability of this forecast record. High confidence forecasts are used for firm operational commitments; low confidence forecasts trigger contingency planning.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS Forecast Confidence Guidance; DTN Weather Services

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this forecast record was first ingested into the agricultural data lakehouse. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer processing compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; SOX Audit Trail Requirements; FSMA Record-Keeping

attributes.name: dew_point_c
attributes.description: Forecast dew point temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Used in disease pressure models (e.g., fungal blight risk) and to assess condensation risk on crops and equipment.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; IPM Disease Forecasting Models

attributes.name: elevation_m
attributes.description: Elevation of the forecast location above mean sea level in meters. Influences temperature lapse rate adjustments, frost risk calculations, and ET evapotranspiration estimates for high-altitude agricultural fields.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; Esri ArcGIS Terrain Analysis

attributes.name: et_forecast_mm
attributes.description: Forecast reference evapotranspiration (ET) in millimeters for the valid period, calculated using the FAO Penman-Monteith method. Primary input for irrigation scheduling decisions and water resource management in Climate FieldView and Trimble Ag Software.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56 (Penman-Monteith); USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: external_forecast_ref
attributes.description: Externally assigned identifier or reference code from the source forecast provider (e.g., NOAA NWS product ID, DTN forecast package ID, Climate FieldView forecast run ID). Enables traceability back to the originating provider record for dispute resolution and data quality audits.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS Product Identification; DTN Weather Services; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: forecast_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the forecast record. Active forecasts are in use for operational decisions; superseded forecasts have been replaced by a newer issue; expired forecasts have passed their valid period; cancelled forecasts were withdrawn by the provider.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services

attributes.name: forecast_type
attributes.description: Temporal resolution and horizon of the forecast record. Hourly forecasts support spray window scheduling; daily and 7-day support planting window decisions; seasonal forecasts align with WASDE outlooks and crop insurance documentation.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS Forecast Products; DTN Weather Services; WASDE (USDA)

attributes.name: freeze_risk
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether forecast minimum temperature is at or below -2.2°C (28°F), triggering a hard freeze alert. Distinguishes from frost risk for crop damage severity classification and crop insurance loss event documentation.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS Freeze Warning Criteria; USDA RMA Crop Insurance; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: frost_risk
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether forecast minimum temperature is at or below 0°C, triggering a frost alert. Supports frost protection decisions including irrigation-based frost protection, smudge pot activation, and harvest acceleration.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS Frost/Freeze Advisories; USDA NRCS; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: gdd_base_temp_c
attributes.business_glossary_term: Growing Degree Day (GDD) Base Temperature Celsius
attributes.description: Base temperature in degrees Celsius used in the GDD growing degree day calculation for this forecast record. Varies by crop species (e.g., 10°C for corn, 4.4°C for wheat). Ensures GDD values are interpreted correctly for the target crop.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView; Crop-Specific GDD Standards

attributes.name: gdd_forecast
attributes.description: Forecast growing degree day accumulation for the valid period, calculated from forecast max and min temperatures relative to a crop-specific base temperature. Supports crop development stage prediction, pest emergence timing, and planting window optimization.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView; NOAA NWS Agricultural Weather

attributes.name: horizon_hours
attributes.description: Number of hours from the issued timestamp to the end of the forecast valid period. Indicates how far into the future the forecast extends, supporting confidence assessment and operational planning lead time.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services

attributes.name: humidity_pct
attributes.description: Forecast relative humidity as a percentage for the valid period. Influences fungal disease pressure prediction, spray efficacy windows, and ET evapotranspiration calculations for irrigation scheduling.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; USDA NRCS; IPM Guidelines

attributes.name: issued_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the forecast was officially issued or published by the source provider. Used to determine forecast freshness and to sequence superseding forecast versions. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; ISO 8601

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Decimal latitude coordinate of the forecast location or field polygon centroid. Used for spatial alignment with GIS field maps and IoT sensor networks. Expressed in decimal degrees (WGS84).
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS; GPS/RTK Positioning Standards; WGS84

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Decimal longitude coordinate of the forecast location or field polygon centroid. Used for spatial alignment with GIS field maps and IoT sensor networks. Expressed in decimal degrees (WGS84).
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS; GPS/RTK Positioning Standards; WGS84

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the numerical weather prediction model used to generate this forecast (e.g., GFS 16.3.0, NAM 4.1, ECMWF CY47R3). Enables traceability and reproducibility of forecast-driven agricultural decisions for audit and compliance purposes.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS NWP Model Documentation; ECMWF; DTN Weather Services

attributes.name: precip_amount_mm
attributes.description: Forecast total precipitation amount in millimeters for the valid period. Used for irrigation scheduling decisions, soil moisture modeling, and crop insurance documentation under USDA Risk Management Agency guidelines.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; USDA RMA Crop Insurance; FSMA

attributes.name: precip_probability_pct
attributes.description: Forecast probability of measurable precipitation occurring during the valid period, expressed as a percentage (0–100). Key input for spray window scheduling — high probability suppresses pesticide application recommendations per IPM Integrated Pest Management protocols.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; EPA IPM Guidelines

attributes.name: precip_type
attributes.description: Forecast type of precipitation expected during the valid period. Distinguishes rain from snow, hail, or freezing rain, which have different implications for field operations, equipment deployment, and crop damage risk assessment.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services

attributes.name: solar_radiation_mj_m2
attributes.business_glossary_term: Solar Radiation Megajoules Per Square Meter
attributes.description: Forecast incoming solar radiation in megajoules per square meter for the valid period. Direct input to the FAO Penman-Monteith ET calculation and photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) models for crop growth simulation.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; USDA NRCS; NOAA NWS

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Originating data provider or system for this forecast record. Identifies whether the forecast was sourced from DTN Data Transmission Network, NOAA National Weather Service, Climate FieldView, custom IoT field sensors, or WASDE World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates seasonal outlook.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Services; NOAA NWS; Climate FieldView; WASDE (USDA)

attributes.name: spray_window_open
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether forecast conditions (wind speed, precipitation probability, temperature, humidity) meet the criteria for a safe and effective pesticide or herbicide application window. Derived from EPA application guidelines and IPM Integrated Pest Management protocols.
attributes.references: EPA Pesticide Application Standards; IPM Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P.; FSMA

attributes.name: temp_avg_c
attributes.description: Forecast mean air temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Used as the base input for GDD growing degree day accumulation calculations and pest pressure prediction models.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; USDA NRCS

attributes.name: temp_max_c
attributes.description: Forecast maximum air temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Used in growing degree day (GDD) accumulation calculations, heat stress assessments, and crop development stage modeling.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; USDA NRCS; ISO 80000-5

attributes.name: temp_min_c
attributes.description: Forecast minimum air temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Critical for frost and freeze alert generation, PHI pre-harvest interval compliance, and cold stress risk assessment for crops.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; USDA NRCS; ISO 80000-5

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this forecast record was last modified or refreshed in the data lakehouse, such as when a forecast is superseded or corrected by the provider. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; SOX Audit Trail Requirements; FSMA Record-Keeping

attributes.name: wind_direction_deg
attributes.description: Forecast prevailing wind direction in meteorological degrees (0–360, where 0/360 = North). Used in spray drift modeling to protect adjacent fields, buffer zones, and sensitive areas per EPA and GLOBALG.A.P. requirements.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; EPA Spray Drift Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: wind_gust_kmh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Wind Gust Speed Kilometers Per Hour
attributes.description: Forecast maximum wind gust speed in kilometers per hour for the valid period. Used to assess equipment safety thresholds for aerial application and tall crop operations.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; EPA Pesticide Application Standards; OSHA

attributes.name: wind_speed_kmh
attributes.description: Forecast average wind speed in kilometers per hour for the valid period. Critical for spray window determination — wind speeds above threshold trigger spray application restrictions per EPA and REI Restricted Entry Interval guidelines.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; EPA Pesticide Application Standards; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: valid_from
attributes.description: Start of the period for which this forecast is valid. For hourly forecasts this is the start of the forecast hour; for daily forecasts it is the start of the forecast day. Used to align forecast data with field operation scheduling windows.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; ISO 8601

attributes.name: valid_to
attributes.description: End of the period for which this forecast is valid. Defines the forecast window boundary for planting, spraying, and irrigation scheduling decisions.
attributes.references: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; ISO 8601

products.name: growing_degree_day
products.description: Growing Degree Day (GDD) accumulation record tracking heat unit accumulation for a specific crop, field, and growing season. Stores daily GDD calculated from min/max temperature against crop-specific base and upper threshold temperatures, cumulative GDD to date, target GDD milestones (emergence, silking, maturity), and deviation from historical norms. Critical for crop development stage prediction, PHI compliance, and harvest timing decisions.
products.reference: USDA GDD Calculation Method / Climate FieldView GDD Tracker

attributes.name: growing_degree_day_id
attributes.description: Primary key for growing_degree_day

attributes.name: climate_normal_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.climate_normal. Business justification: GDD accumulation records compare actual heat unit accumulation against historical averages. growing_degree_day has historical_avg_gdd and gdd_deviation — these reference historical normal values. Link
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: field_crop_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the field crop plan governing the crop variety and management practices for which GDD accumulation is being tracked.
attributes.references: Trimble Ag Software; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: Reference to the agricultural field for which GDD accumulation is being tracked. Links to the field/land parcel master record.
attributes.references: GLOBALG.A.P. IFA Standard; Esri ArcGIS Field Registry

attributes.name: growing_season_id
attributes.description: Reference to the growing season during which GDD accumulation is recorded. Aligns with crop planning and seasonal crop management cycles.
attributes.references: USDA NASS Crop Calendar; Granular Farm Management

attributes.name: planting_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to crop.planting_event. Business justification: GDD accumulation is anchored to the actual planting date from the planting event. Linking growing_degree_day to planting_event provides the precise planting date anchor for GDD calculations, replacing
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: seed_variety_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.seed_variety. Business justification: GDD accumulation thresholds (gdd_to_emergence, gdd_to_silking, gdd_to_maturity) and predicted_maturity_date are seed-variety-specific parameters. Agronomic yield forecasting and harvest scheduling req
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor providing the temperature data used to calculate daily GDD values.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feed; Climate FieldView IoT Integration

attributes.name: accumulation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the GDD accumulation record for this crop and field. 'active' indicates ongoing accumulation; 'paused' indicates temporary suspension (e.g., dormancy period); 'terminated' indicates season ended by frost or crop failure; 'completed' indicates crop reached maturity.
attributes.references: Granular Farm Management; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: base_temperature_c
attributes.description: Crop-specific minimum threshold temperature in degrees Celsius below which crop development does not occur. For corn this is typically 10°C (50°F); for wheat 0°C (32°F). Used as the lower bound in GDD calculation.
attributes.references: USDA ARS Crop Heat Unit Standards; Iowa State University Extension

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: The mathematical method used to calculate daily GDD values. 'standard' uses simple average of min/max temperature minus base; 'modified' applies upper threshold cap; 'baskerville_emin' uses sine curve interpolation for more accurate results.
attributes.references: USDA Agricultural Research Service; Iowa State University Extension GDD Methodology

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this GDD accumulation record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and Silver layer processing tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; SOX Data Audit Requirements; FSMA Record-Keeping

attributes.name: crop_type
attributes.description: The type of crop for which GDD accumulation is being tracked (e.g., corn, soybeans, wheat, cotton). Determines the applicable base and upper threshold temperatures. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: corn|soybeans|wheat|cotton|sorghum|sunflower|barley|canola|rice|alfalfa — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: USDA NASS Crop Classification; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: cumulative_gdd
attributes.description: Running total of heat units accumulated from the planting date or season start date through the record date. Used to predict crop development stage and estimate time to maturity.
attributes.references: USDA NASS; Climate FieldView; Granular Farm Management

attributes.name: current_growth_stage
attributes.description: Estimated crop development stage derived from cumulative GDD accumulation (e.g., VE, V6, VT, R1, R6 for corn; VC, V1, R1, R7, R8 for soybeans). Used for agronomic decision-making, spray window compliance, and PHI tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: VE|V1|V2|V3|V4|V5|V6|VT|R1|R2|R3|R4|R5|R6|R7|R8 — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: USDA ARS Crop Growth Stage Classification; Iowa State University Extension

attributes.name: daily_gdd
attributes.description: Heat units accumulated on the record date, calculated as the average of adjusted min/max temperatures minus the base temperature. Negative values are set to zero. Expressed in degree-days (°C-days or °F-days per calculation method).
attributes.references: USDA ARS GDD Methodology; Iowa State University Extension; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Quality control indicator for the temperature observations used in GDD calculation. 'good' indicates validated sensor data; 'estimated' indicates gap-filled or interpolated values; 'suspect' indicates values outside expected range pending review; 'missing' indicates no data available; 'corrected' indicates post-processing adjustment applied.
attributes.references: WMO Data Quality Standards; NOAA Quality Control Procedures; ISO 22000

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Origin of the temperature data used to calculate the daily GDD value. Indicates whether data came from a physical weather station, IoT field sensor, DTN commercial weather feed, Climate FieldView platform, manual entry, or spatial interpolation.
attributes.references: DTN Data Transmission Network; Climate FieldView; IoT Integration Standards

attributes.name: forecast_gdd_30day
attributes.description: Projected GDD accumulation over the next 30 calendar days based on extended weather forecast data. Used for medium-term harvest planning, logistics coordination, and crop insurance monitoring.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feed; NOAA CPC 30-Day Outlook; WASDE

attributes.name: forecast_gdd_7day
attributes.description: Projected GDD accumulation over the next 7 calendar days based on weather forecast data from DTN or Climate FieldView. Used for short-term irrigation scheduling, spray window planning, and harvest timing decisions.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feed; Climate FieldView Forecast Integration; USDA NASS

attributes.name: frost_event_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a frost or freeze event occurred on the record date (minimum temperature at or below 0°C / 32°F). Critical for crop damage assessment, insurance claims, and replanting decisions.
attributes.references: USDA RMA Crop Insurance; NOAA Frost/Freeze Advisories; APHIS

attributes.name: gdd_deviation
attributes.description: Difference between the current cumulative GDD and the historical average cumulative GDD for the same date and location. Positive values indicate above-normal heat accumulation; negative values indicate below-normal accumulation. Critical for crop insurance documentation and yield forecasting.
attributes.references: NOAA Climate Normals; USDA RMA Crop Insurance Standards; WASDE

attributes.name: gdd_percentile_rank
attributes.description: Percentile rank of the current cumulative GDD relative to the historical distribution for the same crop, location, and calendar date. A value of 90 means the current season is warmer than 90% of historical seasons. Supports climate risk assessment and crop insurance documentation.
attributes.references: NOAA Climate Normals; USDA RMA Actuarial Data

attributes.name: gdd_to_emergence
attributes.description: Crop-specific cumulative GDD milestone required to reach the emergence (VE) growth stage. Used to predict emergence date and validate actual emergence observations against heat unit accumulation.
attributes.references: USDA ARS Crop Development Models; Iowa State University Extension

attributes.name: gdd_to_maturity
attributes.description: Crop-specific cumulative GDD milestone required to reach physiological maturity (black layer for corn, R8 for soybeans). Used for harvest timing decisions, crop insurance documentation, and logistics planning.
attributes.references: USDA ARS Crop Maturity Models; FSMA Harvest Records; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: gdd_to_silking
attributes.description: Crop-specific cumulative GDD milestone required to reach the silking (R1) or equivalent flowering growth stage. Critical for pollination timing, spray window management, and PHI compliance planning.
attributes.references: USDA ARS Corn Development Models; Iowa State University Extension

attributes.name: historical_avg_gdd
attributes.description: Long-term historical average cumulative GDD for the same crop, field location, and calendar date, typically based on a 30-year climate normal. Used as the baseline for deviation analysis and climate risk assessment.
attributes.references: NOAA 30-Year Climate Normals; USDA NASS Historical Data; WASDE

attributes.name: killing_frost_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a killing frost event occurred on the record date (minimum temperature at or below -2.2°C / 28°F for a sustained period). A killing frost terminates the growing season and stops GDD accumulation. Triggers crop insurance documentation requirements.
attributes.references: USDA RMA Crop Insurance Standards; NOAA Freeze Warning Criteria; APHIS

attributes.name: phi_compliance_stage_reached
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) Compliance Stage Reached Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the crop has reached the growth stage at which Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) restrictions for applied agrochemicals become active, as determined by cumulative GDD. Critical for food safety compliance and EPA/FDA regulatory adherence.
attributes.references: EPA Pre-Harvest Interval Regulations; FDA FSMA; GLOBALG.A.P. IFA Standard

attributes.name: predicted_maturity_date
attributes.description: Estimated calendar date when the crop will reach physiological maturity based on current cumulative GDD and historical or forecast temperature trends. Supports harvest scheduling and supply chain planning.
attributes.references: Climate FieldView Predictive Analytics; USDA NASS

attributes.name: record_date
attributes.description: Calendar date for which the daily Growing Degree Day (GDD) value is calculated. Represents the specific day of temperature observation.
attributes.references: USDA NASS; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: season_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which cumulative GDD accumulation begins for this crop and field. Typically the planting date or a standardized calendar date (e.g., January 1 for winter crops). Defines the accumulation window.
attributes.references: USDA NASS Crop Calendar; Climate FieldView Planting Records

attributes.name: spray_window_open
attributes.description: Indicates whether the current crop growth stage (as determined by cumulative GDD) is within an approved spray application window for pesticides or fungicides. Derived from GDD-based growth stage and PHI/REI compliance rules.
attributes.references: EPA Pesticide Registration; GLOBALG.A.P. IFA; Trimble Ag Software Spray Planning

attributes.name: temperature_avg_c
attributes.description: Mean daily air temperature in degrees Celsius, calculated as the average of the minimum and maximum temperatures for the record date. Intermediate value used in standard GDD calculation.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feed; WMO Meteorological Standards

attributes.name: temperature_max_c
attributes.description: Observed maximum air temperature in degrees Celsius recorded at the weather station or field sensor for the record date. Used as the upper bound in daily GDD calculation.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feed; WMO Meteorological Standards; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: temperature_min_c
attributes.description: Observed minimum air temperature in degrees Celsius recorded at the weather station or field sensor for the record date. Used as the lower bound in daily GDD calculation.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feed; WMO Meteorological Standards; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: temperature_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure used for all temperature values and GDD calculations in this record. 'celsius' for metric (°C-days); 'fahrenheit' for imperial (°F-days). Ensures consistent interpretation across systems and regions.
attributes.references: ISO 80000-5 Thermodynamics; USDA Metric Conversion Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this GDD accumulation record was last modified, such as when temperature data was corrected, quality flags were updated, or forecast values were refreshed.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; SOX Data Audit Requirements; FSMA Record-Keeping

attributes.name: upper_threshold_temperature_c
attributes.description: Crop-specific maximum temperature ceiling in degrees Celsius above which additional heat does not accelerate crop development. For corn this is typically 30°C (86°F). Temperatures above this are capped at this value in modified GDD calculations.
attributes.references: USDA ARS Crop Heat Unit Standards; Iowa State University Extension

products.name: evapotranspiration
products.description: Evapotranspiration (ET) calculation and weather-driven water balance record for a field or irrigation zone. Computed using the Penman-Monteith or Hargreaves method from observed or forecast weather inputs. Stores reference ET (ETo), crop ET (ETc) adjusted by crop coefficient (Kc), soil water deficit, ET deficit, soil moisture target, precipitation credit applied, recommended irrigation volume (acre-inches), irrigation method suitability (drip, pivot, flood), and scheduled irrigation date/time when weather-driven scheduling is active. SSOT for weather-derived water balance calculations and ET-based irrigation recommendations that feed irrigation scheduling systems (John Deere Operations Center, Trimble Ag VRA) and water resource management compliance reporting.
products.reference: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET Standard

attributes.name: evapotranspiration_id
attributes.description: Primary key for evapotranspiration

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: Reference to the agricultural field or irrigation zone for which this ET calculation was performed. Links to the field master record in the land and soil domain.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center field mapping; Trimble Ag Software field planning

attributes.name: growing_season_id
attributes.description: Reference to the growing season during which this ET calculation applies, enabling seasonal water balance tracking and crop coefficient (Kc) stage alignment.
attributes.references: Granular Farm Management; Climate FieldView planting and harvest data analytics

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor that provided the meteorological inputs used in this ET calculation. May be a physical station or a virtual grid-point from DTN weather feeds.
attributes.references: DTN Data Transmission Network weather feed; Climate FieldView; IoT sensor integration

attributes.name: calculation_date
attributes.description: The calendar date for which this evapotranspiration calculation was computed. Represents the real-world observation or forecast date, not the record creation date. Used for daily water balance tracking and irrigation scheduling.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56 (Penman-Monteith); USDA NRCS irrigation scheduling guidelines

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: The scientific method used to compute reference evapotranspiration (ETo). Penman-Monteith (FAO-56) is the USDA and FAO standard; Hargreaves is used when solar radiation data is unavailable. Drives traceability and comparability of ET values.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; USDA NRCS; ASCE Standardized Reference ET Equation

attributes.name: calculation_status
attributes.description: Lifecycle status of this ET calculation record. 'computed' indicates automated calculation; 'validated' indicates agronomist review; 'superseded' indicates a newer recalculation replaced this record; 'error' indicates a failed computation requiring review.
attributes.references: Granular Farm Management; John Deere Operations Center; FSMA water management records

attributes.name: calculation_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when this ET calculation record was computed or ingested into the system. Supports audit trail and distinguishes multiple intraday recalculations for the same date.
attributes.references: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer audit conventions

attributes.name: crop_coefficient
attributes.description: Dimensionless crop coefficient (Kc) applied to reference ET to derive crop-specific ET. Value varies by crop growth stage (initial, mid-season, late-season) per FAO-56 tables. Sourced from crop plan or agronomist input.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56 Kc tables; USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: crop_et_mm
attributes.description: Crop evapotranspiration (ETc) in millimetres, calculated as ETo × Kc. Represents the actual water demand of the specific crop at its current growth stage. Primary input to irrigation scheduling and water balance calculations.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; USDA NRCS irrigation scheduling; GLOBALG.A.P. water management

attributes.name: crop_growth_stage
attributes.description: The phenological growth stage of the crop at the time of this ET calculation, used to select the appropriate crop coefficient (Kc) from FAO-56 tables. Stage progression drives changes in water demand throughout the season.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56 Kc stage definitions; BBCH scale; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: cumulative_et_season_mm
attributes.description: Running cumulative crop ET (ETc) in millimetres from the start of the growing season to the calculation date. Used for seasonal water budget tracking, crop insurance documentation, and water use compliance reporting.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS seasonal water budget; FSMA water management records; GLOBALG.A.P.; crop insurance documentation

attributes.name: cumulative_irrigation_season_mm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Seasonal Irrigation Applied in Millimetres
attributes.description: Running cumulative irrigation water applied in millimetres from the start of the growing season to the calculation date. Compared against cumulative ET to assess irrigation efficiency and water use compliance.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; GLOBALG.A.P. water management; EPA water use reporting; ISO 14001

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: Numeric quality score (0–100) reflecting the completeness and reliability of the weather input data used in this ET calculation. Lower scores indicate missing inputs (e.g., estimated solar radiation, gap-filled humidity) that reduce confidence in the ET result.
attributes.references: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer data quality standards; GLOBALG.A.P. data integrity; ISO 22000

attributes.name: data_source_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the weather inputs used in this ET calculation were derived from observed station data, weather forecast models, spatially interpolated grid data, or satellite-derived estimates. Affects confidence in irrigation recommendations.
attributes.references: DTN Data Transmission Network; Climate FieldView; USDA NRCS; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: effective_precipitation_mm
attributes.description: The portion of total precipitation credited toward meeting crop ET demand after accounting for runoff, deep percolation, and interception losses. Calculated per USDA SCS method. Reduces the net irrigation requirement.
attributes.references: USDA SCS Effective Rainfall method; FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 25; NRCS

attributes.name: et_deficit_mm
attributes.description: Daily ET deficit in millimetres, calculated as ETc minus effective precipitation. Represents the net water demand that must be met by irrigation for the calculation date. Negative values indicate precipitation surplus.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; USDA NRCS irrigation scheduling guidelines

attributes.name: frost_risk_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether minimum temperature conditions on the calculation date meet or fall below the frost threshold for the crop type. Triggers frost/freeze alerts in irrigation scheduling systems and supports crop insurance documentation.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS frost date tables; Climate FieldView; crop insurance USDA RMA guidelines

attributes.name: irrigation_method
attributes.description: The irrigation delivery method applicable to this field and ET recommendation. Determines application efficiency factors and scheduling logic. Drip and subsurface drip have higher application efficiency than flood or sprinkler systems.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; Trimble Ag Software; USDA NRCS irrigation method classifications; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: max_temperature_c
attributes.business_glossary_term: Maximum Air Temperature in Degrees Celsius
attributes.description: Maximum daily air temperature in degrees Celsius used as a weather input to the ET calculation. Required by both Penman-Monteith and Hargreaves methods. Sourced from weather station or DTN feed.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; DTN Data Transmission Network; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: mean_temperature_c
attributes.business_glossary_term: Mean Air Temperature in Degrees Celsius
attributes.description: Mean daily air temperature in degrees Celsius, calculated as the average of maximum and minimum temperatures. Used in Hargreaves ET method and growing degree day (GDD) accumulation calculations.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView GDD tracking

attributes.name: min_temperature_c
attributes.business_glossary_term: Minimum Air Temperature in Degrees Celsius
attributes.description: Minimum daily air temperature in degrees Celsius used as a weather input to the ET calculation. Required by both Penman-Monteith and Hargreaves methods. Also used for frost risk assessment.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; DTN Data Transmission Network; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text agronomist or system notes associated with this ET calculation record, capturing manual overrides, data quality observations, or irrigation scheduling decisions that deviate from the automated recommendation.
attributes.references: Granular Farm Management; GLOBALG.A.P. record-keeping requirements; FSMA documentation

attributes.name: precipitation_mm
attributes.description: Total precipitation (rainfall) recorded or forecast for the calculation date in millimetres. Used as a credit against crop ET demand in the daily water balance calculation.
attributes.references: DTN Data Transmission Network; USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView; WASDE

attributes.name: recommended_irrigation_acre_in
attributes.description: Weather-driven irrigation recommendation expressed in acre-inches per acre, derived from the ET deficit and soil water deficit. Primary output consumed by John Deere Operations Center and Trimble Ag VRA for irrigation scheduling and variable rate application prescriptions.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; Trimble Ag VRA; USDA NRCS; GLOBALG.A.P. water management

attributes.name: recommended_irrigation_mm
attributes.description: Weather-driven irrigation recommendation expressed in millimetres, the SI unit equivalent of the acre-inch recommendation. Used for international reporting, water resource compliance, and integration with metric-based irrigation controllers.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; ISO 14001 Environmental Management; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: reference_et_mm
attributes.description: Reference evapotranspiration (ETo) in millimetres for the calculation date, representing the ET demand of a standardised reference crop (short grass or alfalfa). The foundational output of the Penman-Monteith or Hargreaves equation. Used as the basis for crop-specific ET adjustment.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; ASCE Standardized Reference ET Equation; USDA NRCS

attributes.name: relative_humidity_pct
attributes.description: Mean daily relative humidity as a percentage, used in the Penman-Monteith ET calculation to determine vapour pressure deficit. High humidity reduces ET demand; low humidity increases it.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; DTN Data Transmission Network; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: scheduled_irrigation_date
attributes.description: The recommended calendar date on which irrigation should be applied based on the ET-driven water balance calculation. Populated when weather-driven scheduling is active. Null when no irrigation is currently recommended.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center irrigation scheduling; Trimble Ag VRA; USDA NRCS

attributes.name: scheduled_irrigation_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise scheduled start date and time for the recommended irrigation event, used when automated irrigation controllers require time-of-day scheduling. Null when only date-level scheduling is active.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; Trimble Ag Software; IoT irrigation controller integration

attributes.name: soil_moisture_target_pct
attributes.description: Target soil moisture level as a percentage of field capacity for this field and crop stage. Used as the trigger threshold for irrigation scheduling. Typically set between 50–70% of available water capacity depending on crop stress tolerance.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; Trimble Ag Software VRA prescriptions

attributes.name: soil_water_deficit_mm
attributes.description: Cumulative soil water deficit in millimetres representing the difference between field capacity and current soil moisture content. Positive values indicate irrigation need. Updated daily using the FAO-56 water balance model.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56 water balance; USDA NRCS; Trimble Ag VRA

attributes.name: solar_radiation_mj_m2
attributes.business_glossary_term: Solar Radiation in Megajoules per Square Metre
attributes.description: Daily incoming solar radiation in megajoules per square metre (MJ/m²), a primary driver of ET demand in the Penman-Monteith equation. Sourced from weather station pyranometer or estimated from sunshine hours and cloud cover.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; WMO; DTN Data Transmission Network

attributes.name: spray_window_suitable
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether weather conditions on the calculation date are suitable for pesticide or fertilizer spray application, based on wind speed, temperature, humidity, and precipitation thresholds. Supports Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and EPA/REI compliance.
attributes.references: EPA pesticide application weather requirements; IPM guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P.; Trimble Ag Software spray window logic

attributes.name: vapour_pressure_deficit_kpa
attributes.description: Vapour pressure deficit (VPD) in kilopascals, representing the difference between saturated and actual vapour pressure. A key intermediate variable in the Penman-Monteith ET calculation and an indicator of atmospheric drying demand on crops.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; ASCE Standardized Reference ET; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: water_stress_index
attributes.description: Dimensionless water stress coefficient (Ks) ranging from 0 to 1, representing the degree of crop water stress due to soil moisture deficit. A value of 1 indicates no stress; values below 1 indicate stress-adjusted ET. Used in FAO-56 dual crop coefficient approach.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56 Ks calculation; USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: wind_speed_ms
attributes.business_glossary_term: Wind Speed in Metres per Second
attributes.description: Mean daily wind speed at 2-metre height in metres per second, a required input to the Penman-Monteith ET equation. Higher wind speeds increase ET demand by enhancing vapour transport from the crop canopy.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; DTN Data Transmission Network; WMO meteorological standards

products.name: frost_alert
products.description: Frost and freeze event alert record generated when forecast or observed temperatures fall below crop-specific critical thresholds. Captures alert type (advisory/watch/warning), predicted low temperature, frost probability, affected field or geographic zone, crop vulnerability rating, recommended protective actions (frost cloth, irrigation frost protection), and alert source (DTN, NWS). Supports crop protection decision-making and insurance loss documentation.
products.reference: NOAA Frost/Freeze Advisory Standard

attributes.name: frost_alert_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each frost or freeze alert record. Primary key for the frost_alert data product in the weather domain.
attributes.references: Internal Data Architecture Standard

attributes.name: alert_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.weather_alert. Business justification: A frost alert is a specialized type of weather alert. When NWS or DTN issues a broader weather alert that includes frost/freeze conditions, the frost_alert record should reference the parent weather_a
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: crew_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.crew. Business justification: Frost alert response is a named crew-level operational process: when a frost alert fires, the field crew responsible for frost protection (irrigation activation, row cover deployment) must be identifi
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: crop_enterprise_budget_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.crop_enterprise_budget. Business justification: Frost events directly cause yield loss and revenue shortfalls requiring crop enterprise budget variance analysis and revision. Farm financial analysts must trace frost alerts to the affected budget to
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific agricultural field or management zone affected by the frost alert. Enables field-level crop protection decision-making and insurance loss documentation per FSMA traceability requirements.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; Esri ArcGIS; FSMA Traceability Rule

attributes.name: growing_season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to crop.growing_season. Business justification: Frost alerts are issued for specific crop growth stages within a growing season. Linking frost_alert to growing_season supports season-level frost risk tracking, insurance claim relevance determinatio
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: seed_variety_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.seed_variety. Business justification: Frost protection decisions and estimated crop loss calculations depend on the specific seed variety's cold tolerance rating and growth stage vulnerability. RMA crop insurance loss adjustment requires
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor that observed or forecast the frost/freeze condition. Links to the weather station master record for geographic and instrument metadata.
attributes.references: NOAA Weather Station Network; DTN; IoT Integration Standards

attributes.name: triggering_forecast_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.forecast. Business justification: Frost alerts are generated when forecast temperatures fall below crop-critical thresholds. Linking frost_alert to the triggering forecast record provides full traceability from alert back to the sourc
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: triggering_observation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.observation. Business justification: Frost alerts can be triggered by observed (actual) temperatures falling below critical thresholds, not just forecast data. frost_alert has observed_low_temp_c which is an observed value. Linking to th
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.weather_zone. Business justification: NWS and DTN frost alerts are issued at the geographic zone level. frost_alert has geographic_zone_code (STRING) which is a denormalized reference to weather_zone.zone_code. Adding weather_zone_id FK n
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: acknowledged_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the farm manager, agronomist, or operations staff member who acknowledged the frost alert. Supports accountability tracking and FSMA food safety plan documentation.
attributes.references: FSMA Preventive Controls Rule; GLOBALG.A.P.; SOX Internal Controls

attributes.name: acknowledgement_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when a farm manager or agronomist acknowledged receipt of the frost alert. Used for operational response time tracking and compliance documentation under FSMA food safety planning requirements.
attributes.references: FSMA Preventive Controls Rule; GLOBALG.A.P.; SOP Compliance

attributes.name: affected_area_ha
attributes.description: Total agricultural area affected by the frost event, expressed in hectares. Used for insurance loss quantification, resource allocation for protective actions, and USDA reporting.
attributes.references: USDA NASS; USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA); GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: alert_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Forecast or observed end date and time of the frost or freeze event window. Marks when temperatures are expected to rise above the critical threshold. Used for operational planning and insurance documentation.
attributes.references: NWS; DTN Weather Services; ISO 8601

attributes.name: alert_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for agronomist or farm manager observations, supplementary meteorological context, protective action outcomes, or post-event damage assessment notes associated with the frost alert.
attributes.references: GLOBALG.A.P.; Good Agricultural Practices (GAP); FSMA Recordkeeping Requirements

attributes.name: alert_source
attributes.description: Originating system or data provider that generated the frost alert. DTN (Data Transmission Network) and NWS (National Weather Service) are primary external sources; Climate FieldView and IoT sensors provide field-level triggers; Manual indicates agronomist-entered alerts.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Services; National Weather Service (NWS); Climate FieldView Integration

attributes.name: alert_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Forecast or observed start date and time of the frost or freeze event window. Used for spray window planning, irrigation frost protection scheduling, and field crew deployment timing.
attributes.references: NWS; DTN Weather Services; ISO 8601

attributes.name: alert_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the frost alert. 'active' indicates the alert is in effect; 'acknowledged' means a farm manager has confirmed receipt; 'expired' means the alert window has passed; 'cancelled' means the threat did not materialize; 'superseded' means a newer alert replaced this one.
attributes.references: National Weather Service (NWS) Alert Lifecycle Standards; USDA

attributes.name: alert_type
attributes.description: Classification of the frost or freeze alert severity following NWS conventions. 'advisory' indicates frost possible; 'watch' indicates conditions favorable for frost/freeze; 'warning' indicates frost/freeze imminent or occurring; 'freeze_warning' indicates temperatures at or below 28°F for 2+ hours.
attributes.references: National Weather Service (NWS) Frost/Freeze Alert Classification; USDA

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording when the frost alert record was first ingested and persisted in the data lakehouse. Used for data lineage, SLA monitoring, and audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; SOX Audit Trail Requirements; FSMA Traceability Rule

attributes.name: critical_threshold_temp_c
attributes.description: Crop-specific critical temperature threshold in degrees Celsius below which significant crop damage is expected. Derived from crop type and growth stage; used to determine alert severity and trigger protective actions.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Crop Damage Thresholds; GLOBALG.A.P.; Codex Alimentarius

attributes.name: crop_vulnerability_rating
attributes.description: Assessed vulnerability of the affected crop to the forecast frost event, combining crop type, growth stage, and forecast temperature. Drives urgency of protective action recommendations and insurance claim pre-notification.
attributes.references: USDA Risk Management Agency; GLOBALG.A.P.; Codex Alimentarius Commission

attributes.name: dew_point_temp_c
attributes.description: Forecast or observed dew point temperature in degrees Celsius. When dew point falls below 0°C, frost deposition on plant surfaces is likely. Critical input for frost type determination and crop damage assessment.
attributes.references: World Meteorological Organization (WMO); NWS; DTN Weather Services

attributes.name: estimated_crop_loss_pct
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of crop yield loss attributable to the frost event, assessed post-event by agronomists or automated damage models. Used for insurance claim quantification and WASDE impact reporting. Null until post-event assessment is completed.
attributes.references: USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA); WASDE Report; Federal Crop Insurance Act

attributes.name: forecast_low_temp_c
attributes.description: Predicted minimum air temperature in degrees Celsius for the alert period. This is the principal quantitative measurement driving the frost alert. Used to assess crop vulnerability and determine protective action thresholds.
attributes.references: World Meteorological Organization (WMO); DTN Weather Services; NWS

attributes.name: frost_duration_hours
attributes.description: Expected or observed duration of sub-threshold temperatures in hours. Critical for assessing cumulative crop damage exposure; freeze warnings typically require 2+ hours below 28°F for severe damage classification.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; NWS Freeze Warning Criteria; Codex Alimentarius

attributes.name: frost_probability_pct
attributes.description: Probabilistic forecast of frost occurrence expressed as a percentage (0.00–100.00). Sourced from DTN or NWS ensemble forecast models. Used to calibrate alert urgency and protective action decisions.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Services; NWS Probabilistic Forecasting; WMO

attributes.name: frost_type
attributes.description: Classification of the frost event mechanism. 'radiation' frost occurs on calm, clear nights due to radiative cooling; 'advection' frost results from cold air mass movement; 'evaporation' frost occurs due to rapid moisture evaporation. Determines appropriate protective measures.
attributes.references: World Meteorological Organization (WMO); USDA NRCS; NWS

attributes.name: gdd_impact_estimate
attributes.description: Estimated reduction in Growing Degree Day (GDD) accumulation attributable to the frost event. GDD accumulation drives crop phenology and maturity timing; frost-induced GDD loss affects harvest scheduling and yield forecasting in Climate FieldView.
attributes.references: USDA NASS Growing Degree Day Methodology; Climate FieldView; Granular Farm Management

attributes.name: insurance_claim_relevant
attributes.description: Indicates whether this frost alert event is relevant for crop insurance loss documentation. When True, the alert record is flagged for retention and inclusion in USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) crop insurance claim packages.
attributes.references: USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA); Federal Crop Insurance Act; FSMA

attributes.name: irrigation_frost_protection
attributes.description: Indicates whether overhead irrigation frost protection has been recommended or activated for this alert. Irrigation frost protection uses latent heat of freezing water to protect crops; relevant to irrigation scheduling systems.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Irrigation Management; Good Agricultural Practices (GAP); GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: issued_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the frost alert was officially issued by the source system or meteorological authority. This is the principal real-world event time for the alert, distinct from the record creation audit timestamp.
attributes.references: National Weather Service (NWS); ISO 8601

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate (decimal degrees, WGS84) of the alert centroid or affected field center. Supports GIS-based spatial analysis and precision agriculture mapping in Esri ArcGIS.
attributes.references: WGS84 Coordinate Reference System; Esri ArcGIS; GPS Standards

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate (decimal degrees, WGS84) of the alert centroid or affected field center. Supports GIS-based spatial analysis and precision agriculture mapping in Esri ArcGIS.
attributes.references: WGS84 Coordinate Reference System; Esri ArcGIS; GPS Standards

attributes.name: nws_event_code
attributes.description: External reference identifier assigned by the National Weather Service (NWS) to the corresponding official frost or freeze advisory, watch, or warning. Enables cross-referencing with NWS public alert records for regulatory and insurance documentation.
attributes.references: National Weather Service (NWS) CAP (Common Alerting Protocol); USDA

attributes.name: observed_low_temp_c
attributes.description: Actual recorded minimum air temperature in degrees Celsius as measured by the weather station or IoT sensor during the frost event. Populated post-event; used for insurance loss documentation and model validation.
attributes.references: World Meteorological Organization (WMO); USDA Risk Management Agency; NWS

attributes.name: recommended_action
attributes.description: Primary recommended protective action for the affected field or zone based on alert severity and crop vulnerability. Examples include frost cloth application, overhead irrigation frost protection, wind machine activation, smudge pot deployment, or harvest acceleration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: frost_cloth|overhead_irrigation|wind_machine|smudge_pot|harvest_acceleration|no_action|monitor — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Best Management Practices (BMP); GLOBALG.A.P.; Good Agricultural Practices (GAP)

attributes.name: relative_humidity_pct
attributes.description: Forecast or observed relative humidity percentage at the time of the frost event. Low humidity combined with low temperatures increases frost severity; used in dew point and frost point calculations.
attributes.references: World Meteorological Organization (WMO); DTN Weather Services; NWS

attributes.name: sky_condition
attributes.description: Forecast or observed sky cover condition at the time of the frost event. Clear skies promote radiative cooling and increase frost severity; overcast conditions reduce frost risk by trapping longwave radiation.
attributes.references: World Meteorological Organization (WMO); NWS; DTN Weather Services

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording when the frost alert record was last modified, such as when status changes, forecast updates are received, or protective action outcomes are recorded.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; SOX Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: wind_speed_ms
attributes.description: Forecast or observed wind speed in meters per second at the time of the frost event. Low wind speeds (calm conditions) increase radiation frost risk; used in frost type classification (radiation vs. advection frost).
attributes.references: World Meteorological Organization (WMO); DTN Weather Services; NWS

products.name: precipitation_event
products.description: Discrete severe weather event record capturing precipitation, hail, and high-wind episodes at field or station level. Stores event start/end timestamps, total precipitation amount, peak intensity, storm type (convective, frontal, orographic), hail stone size (inches) and density (stones/sq ft), peak wind gust speed (mph), sustained wind speed, wind direction, Beaufort scale classification, crop lodging risk flag, spray drift risk level, structural damage risk indicator, runoff estimate, soil saturation index, estimated crop damage severity (none/light/moderate/severe), affected acreage, storm track path, and insurance claim trigger flag. SSOT for all field-level severe weather event documentation including precipitation, hail, and wind damage. Used for irrigation adjustments, trafficability assessment, spray window invalidation, crop insurance documentation, USDA disaster reporting, and FSIS compliance.
products.reference: NOAA Precipitation Event Classification

attributes.name: precipitation_event_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each discrete severe weather precipitation event record. Primary key for the precipitation_event data product.
attributes.references: Internal Data Architecture Standard

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: Reference to the agricultural field or land parcel where this precipitation event was observed or estimated. Used for field-level irrigation adjustment and crop damage assessment.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center Field Mapping; Esri ArcGIS Land Parcel

attributes.name: growing_season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to crop.growing_season. Business justification: Precipitation events (hail, flooding) are assessed for crop loss impact within a specific growing season for insurance claim trigger evaluation and USDA disaster reporting. crop_type and crop_growth_s
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor that recorded this precipitation event. Links to the station master record for location and calibration metadata.
attributes.references: NOAA Weather Station Standards; Climate FieldView Integration

attributes.name: affected_acreage
attributes.description: Estimated total acreage impacted by this precipitation event. Used for USDA disaster reporting, crop insurance claim quantification, and field-level damage assessment prioritization.
attributes.references: USDA FSA Disaster Reporting; USDA RMA Crop Insurance; COOL

attributes.name: beaufort_scale
attributes.description: Beaufort wind force scale classification (0–12) derived from sustained wind speed. Provides standardized wind severity classification for spray window invalidation, equipment operation decisions, and insurance documentation.
attributes.references: World Meteorological Organization (WMO) Beaufort Scale; NWS

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this precipitation event record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and SLA compliance tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; SOX Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: crop_damage_severity
attributes.description: Categorical assessment of estimated crop damage severity resulting from this precipitation event. Used for USDA disaster reporting, crop insurance claim documentation, and yield loss forecasting. Severity is assessed based on storm type, hail size, wind speed, and affected crop growth stage.
attributes.references: USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA); USDA FSA Disaster Reporting; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: crop_lodging_risk
attributes.description: Indicates whether wind speed and precipitation conditions during this event meet or exceed thresholds associated with crop lodging (stem breakage or root displacement). True triggers agronomic review and potential yield loss assessment.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Crop Lodging Standards; Granular Farm Management

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Identifies the originating data source system for this precipitation event record. Used for data lineage tracking, quality weighting, and source reconciliation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: iot_sensor|dtn_feed|climate_fieldview|manual_entry|noaa_api|nws_api — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feed Integration; Climate FieldView; IoT Field Sensor Standards; NOAA

attributes.name: event_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the precipitation or severe weather event concluded at the recorded location. Used to calculate event duration and determine trafficability and re-entry windows. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: USDA Disaster Reporting; FSMA; ISO 8601

attributes.name: event_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for this precipitation event, used for cross-referencing with USDA disaster reports, insurance claim documentation, and DTN weather feed records. Format: EVT-YYYYMMDD-NNNN.
attributes.references: USDA Disaster Reporting; DTN Weather Feed; FSMA Compliance

attributes.name: event_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the precipitation or severe weather event began at the recorded location. Principal real-world event time used for spray window invalidation, irrigation scheduling, and insurance claim trigger documentation. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: USDA Disaster Reporting; FSMA; ISO 8601

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the precipitation event record. 'active' indicates the event is ongoing; 'completed' indicates the event has ended and data is finalized; 'cancelled' indicates a false alarm or data retraction; 'under_review' indicates the record is pending quality validation.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: external_event_ref
attributes.description: External system identifier for this event as assigned by the source system (e.g., DTN event ID, NWS storm report number, Climate FieldView event key). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit traceability.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feed; NWS Storm Data Publication; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: hail_density_stones_sqft
attributes.description: Estimated number of hail stones per square foot observed during the event. Combined with hail stone size to determine crop damage severity and insurance claim trigger eligibility. Null when precip_type is not hail or mixed.
attributes.references: USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) Hail Damage Assessment; NOAA

attributes.name: hail_stone_size_in
attributes.description: Maximum observed hail stone diameter in inches during the event. Used to assess structural damage risk to crops, equipment, and infrastructure. Null when precip_type is not hail or mixed.
attributes.references: NOAA Hail Size Classification; USDA Crop Insurance Hail Damage Standards; RMA

attributes.name: insurance_claim_trigger
