attributes.description: Indicates whether this precipitation event meets the threshold criteria to trigger a crop insurance claim under the applicable USDA RMA policy. True initiates the insurance claim documentation workflow and notifies the risk management team.
attributes.references: USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA); Federal Crop Insurance Act; USDA FSA

attributes.name: irrigation_adjustment_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this precipitation event requires adjustment to the active irrigation schedule. True triggers review of ET (Evapotranspiration) balance and irrigation prescription update in the FMIS (Farm Management Information System).
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Irrigation Water Management; Climate FieldView; Trimble Ag Software

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate (WGS84 decimal degrees) of the primary observation point for this precipitation event. Used for spatial analysis, GIS mapping, and cross-referencing with field boundaries in Esri ArcGIS.
attributes.references: WGS84 Coordinate Reference System; Esri ArcGIS; GPS Standards

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate (WGS84 decimal degrees) of the primary observation point for this precipitation event. Used for spatial analysis, GIS mapping, and cross-referencing with field boundaries in Esri ArcGIS.
attributes.references: WGS84 Coordinate Reference System; Esri ArcGIS; GPS Standards

attributes.name: precip_intensity_peak_mm_hr
attributes.description: Maximum instantaneous precipitation rate in millimeters per hour recorded during the event. High peak intensity values indicate elevated runoff risk, soil erosion potential, and spray drift invalidation conditions.
attributes.references: NOAA Precipitation Intensity Standards; USDA NRCS

attributes.name: precip_total_mm
attributes.description: Total accumulated precipitation depth in millimeters recorded during the event. Primary quantitative outcome used for irrigation scheduling adjustments, runoff estimation, soil saturation assessment, and USDA disaster reporting thresholds.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Precipitation Standards; NOAA; ISO 22000

attributes.name: precip_type
attributes.description: Classification of the form of precipitation observed during the event. Determines downstream impact on crop damage assessment, trafficability, and equipment operation windows.
attributes.references: NWS Precipitation Type Classification; USDA Disaster Reporting

attributes.name: runoff_estimate_mm
attributes.description: Estimated surface water runoff depth in millimeters generated by this precipitation event, calculated using USDA NRCS curve number methodology. Used for soil erosion assessment, nutrient loss estimation, and BMP (Best Management Practices) compliance reporting.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Curve Number Runoff Method; EPA BMP Standards; ISO 14001

attributes.name: soil_saturation_index
attributes.description: Dimensionless index (0.00–1.00) representing estimated soil water saturation level following this precipitation event. Values approaching 1.00 indicate near-full saturation, triggering trafficability restrictions and irrigation suspension. Derived from precipitation total, soil type, and antecedent moisture conditions.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Soil Moisture Standards; Trimble Ag Software; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: spray_drift_risk_level
attributes.description: Categorical assessment of spray drift risk based on wind speed, wind direction, and precipitation conditions during the event. Used to invalidate spray windows and ensure compliance with EPA pesticide application restrictions and REI (Restricted Entry Interval) requirements.
attributes.references: EPA Spray Drift Guidelines; FIFRA; GLOBALG.A.P.; IPM Standards

attributes.name: spray_window_invalidated
attributes.description: Indicates whether this precipitation event has invalidated one or more planned spray application windows. True triggers re-scheduling of pesticide or fertilizer applications and PHI (Pre-Harvest Interval) recalculation.
attributes.references: EPA FIFRA Spray Application Standards; GLOBALG.A.P.; IPM Standards

attributes.name: storm_track_path
attributes.description: GIS-encoded storm track path as a WKT (Well-Known Text) LineString representing the movement trajectory of the storm system across the geographic area. Used for spatial analysis of multi-field impact assessment in Esri ArcGIS.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS Geospatial Standards; NWS Storm Track Data; OGC WKT Standard

attributes.name: storm_type
attributes.description: Meteorological classification of the storm system producing the precipitation event. Convective storms are associated with thunderstorms and rapid intensity; frontal storms are associated with weather front passages; orographic storms result from terrain-forced uplift. Used for pest pressure prediction and crop insurance documentation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: convective|frontal|orographic|tropical|extratropical|monsoonal — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: National Weather Service (NWS) Storm Classification; USDA Disaster Reporting

attributes.name: structural_damage_risk
attributes.description: Indicates whether the combination of wind gust speed, hail size, and precipitation intensity during this event poses a risk of structural damage to farm buildings, grain storage, irrigation infrastructure, or equipment. True triggers facility inspection workflow.
attributes.references: USDA Disaster Reporting; OSHA Facility Safety Standards

attributes.name: trafficability_restricted
attributes.description: Indicates whether field trafficability is restricted following this precipitation event due to soil saturation or standing water conditions. True prevents heavy equipment entry and triggers field access hold in the John Deere Operations Center fleet management workflow.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; USDA NRCS Soil Trafficability Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this precipitation event record was last modified. Used for change tracking, data quality monitoring, and incremental data pipeline processing. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; SOX Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: usda_disaster_reportable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this precipitation event qualifies for USDA disaster program reporting under FSA emergency programs. True triggers submission to the USDA Farm Service Agency disaster reporting workflow.
attributes.references: USDA FSA Emergency Loan Programs; USDA Disaster Designation Process

attributes.name: wind_direction_deg
attributes.description: Prevailing wind direction in degrees from true north (0–360) during the event. Used for spray drift risk assessment, storm track path analysis, and field-level impact modeling.
attributes.references: NWS Meteorological Standards; EPA Spray Drift Guidelines

attributes.name: wind_gust_peak_mph
attributes.description: Maximum instantaneous wind gust speed in miles per hour recorded during the event. Used to assess crop lodging risk, spray drift risk, structural damage risk, and Beaufort scale classification.
attributes.references: NWS Wind Speed Standards; Beaufort Scale; EPA Spray Drift Guidelines

attributes.name: wind_speed_sustained_mph
attributes.description: Average sustained wind speed in miles per hour over the event duration. Used alongside peak gust for Beaufort classification, spray window assessment, and crop lodging risk evaluation.
attributes.references: NWS Wind Speed Standards; Beaufort Scale; EPA Spray Drift Guidelines

products.name: spray_window
products.description: Calculated time window record defining meteorologically permissible periods for pesticide, herbicide, or fertilizer application at field level. Stores window start/end datetime, wind speed range, temperature range, humidity range, inversion risk flag, delta-T value, REI (Restricted Entry Interval) compliance status, and EPA/state drift regulation constraint flags. Weather domain SSOT for application-window meteorological feasibility; integrates with crop protection planning workflows for label-compliant scheduling.
products.reference: EPA Pesticide Application Weather Requirements / REI Standards

attributes.name: spray_window_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the spray window record. Primary key for the spray_window data product in the weather domain.
attributes.references: Internal Data Architecture Standard

attributes.name: agrochemical_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.agrochemical_product. Business justification: Spray window compliance validation requires the specific agrochemical product being applied — rei_compliant, rei_hours, phi_days, epa_drift_constraint, and label_compliant on spray_window must be vali
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: crew_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.crew. Business justification: Spray windows are operationally assigned to specific pesticide application crews. Linking spray_window to crew enforces WPS REI compliance, verifies crew pesticide applicator certification, and drives
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: Reference to the agricultural field for which this spray window is calculated. Links to the field master record in the crop management domain.
attributes.references: GLOBALG.A.P. Control Point CB 7.1; FSMA Produce Safety Rule §112

attributes.name: forecast_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.forecast. Business justification: Spray windows are calculated using weather forecast data (wind speed, temperature, humidity, precipitation probability). Linking spray_window to the specific forecast record used during window calcula
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: observation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.observation. Business justification: Spray windows can be calculated from real-time meteorological observations (current wind speed, temperature, humidity, delta-T). Linking spray_window to the specific observation record used during win
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor providing the meteorological data used to calculate this spray window. May reference a physical station or a virtual grid point from DTN weather feeds.
attributes.references: Climate FieldView; DTN Weather Data Feed

attributes.name: application_method
attributes.description: Planned or applicable pesticide/fertilizer application method for this spray window. Different methods have different wind speed, temperature, and drift constraints under EPA and state regulations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ground_boom|aerial|airblast|chemigation|drone|hand_application|fertigation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170; USDA APHIS; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; FAA Drone Regulations

attributes.name: buffer_zone_m
attributes.description: Required no-spray buffer zone distance in metres from field edge to sensitive areas, as determined by product label, EPA registration, and state regulations for this spray window. Operationally enforced during application.
attributes.references: EPA FIFRA Label Requirements; EPA 40 CFR Part 170; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: Qualitative confidence level of the spray window calculation based on forecast model accuracy, data source reliability, and forecast horizon. Used by agronomists to prioritise scheduling decisions.
attributes.references: Climate FieldView; DTN Weather Feed; Trimble Ag Software

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this spray window record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and regulatory documentation requirements.
attributes.references: FSMA §112; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; ISO 22000; SOX Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: delta_t_value
attributes.description: Delta-T (ΔT) is the difference between dry-bulb and wet-bulb temperatures in degrees Celsius, used as the primary indicator of spray droplet evaporation rate and application suitability. Optimal Delta-T range is typically 2–8°C; values outside this range indicate poor spray conditions.
attributes.references: GRDC Spray Decision Guidelines; EPA Drift Reduction Technology; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: dew_point_c
attributes.description: Dew point temperature in degrees Celsius during the spray window. Used alongside Delta-T and humidity to assess spray droplet evaporation conditions and risk of leaf wetness that may affect product uptake.
attributes.references: Climate FieldView; GRDC Spray Decision Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: epa_drift_constraint
attributes.description: Indicates whether EPA drift reduction regulatory constraints are active for this spray window, based on proximity to sensitive areas (water bodies, schools, residential zones) and product-specific drift management requirements under EPA 40 CFR Part 170.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170; EPA Drift Reduction Technology Program; FIFRA

attributes.name: et_mm
attributes.description: Evapotranspiration (ET) in millimetres during the spray window period. High ET rates indicate conditions that accelerate spray droplet evaporation, reducing efficacy and increasing fine-droplet drift risk.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS ET Reference; Climate FieldView; FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56

attributes.name: external_window_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier from the originating external system (Climate FieldView, DTN, Trimble Ag Software) for this spray window record. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit traceability back to the source system.
attributes.references: Climate FieldView; DTN Weather Feed; Trimble Ag Software; FSMA Traceability Rule

attributes.name: forecast_horizon_hours
attributes.description: Number of hours ahead from the calculation timestamp that this spray window is forecast for. Shorter horizons indicate higher confidence; longer horizons are used for advance planning. Null for observation-based windows.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feed; Climate FieldView; WASDE Forecast Standards

attributes.name: gdd_base_temp_c
attributes.description: Base temperature in degrees Celsius used for Growing Degree Day (GDD) accumulation calculations associated with this spray window. GDD thresholds trigger pest pressure predictions and optimal application timing for certain products.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView GDD Models; Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Guidelines

attributes.name: humidity_max_pct
attributes.description: Maximum relative humidity percentage during the spray window. Excessively high humidity can reduce product efficacy for certain fungicides and herbicides and may indicate inversion risk conditions.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: humidity_min_pct
attributes.description: Minimum relative humidity percentage during the spray window. Low humidity increases evaporation of spray droplets, reducing efficacy and increasing drift risk. Label compliance thresholds typically specify minimum humidity levels.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: inversion_risk
attributes.description: Indicates whether atmospheric temperature inversion conditions are present or forecast during the spray window. Temperature inversions trap spray droplets near the ground and cause unpredictable drift; most regulatory bodies and labels prohibit spraying during inversion conditions.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170; USDA NRCS BMP; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: ipm_pest_pressure
attributes.business_glossary_term: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Pest Pressure Level
attributes.description: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) pest pressure classification at the time of the spray window, used to determine application urgency and prioritise scheduling within available windows. Derived from scouting observations and GDD-based pest models.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS IPM Guidelines; EPA Pesticide Registration; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: label_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether all meteorological conditions within this spray window satisfy the agrochemical product label requirements for application (wind speed, temperature, humidity, Delta-T, precipitation-free period). Master compliance flag for regulatory audit purposes.
attributes.references: EPA FIFRA Label Requirements; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; FSMA §112

attributes.name: phi_days
attributes.description: The Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) in days for the planned agrochemical product, representing the minimum number of days that must elapse between the last application and crop harvest. Ensures Maximum Residue Limits (MRL) are not exceeded at harvest.
attributes.references: EPA FIFRA Label Requirements; FDA 21 CFR Part 193; Codex Alimentarius MRL Standards; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: precip_free_hours
attributes.description: Minimum number of hours without precipitation required after application for the planned agrochemical product to achieve label-specified efficacy. Sourced from product label requirements and used to validate window suitability.
attributes.references: EPA FIFRA Label Requirements; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: precip_probability_pct
attributes.description: Forecast probability of precipitation (%) during or immediately following the spray window. High precipitation probability risks product wash-off, reducing efficacy and potentially causing runoff into water bodies. Most labels specify minimum dry periods post-application.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; Climate FieldView; DTN Weather Feed

attributes.name: rei_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the spray window timing satisfies the Restricted Entry Interval (REI) requirements for the planned agrochemical product, ensuring workers cannot re-enter treated areas before the REI expires. Derived from window_end plus the product-specific REI duration.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170 Worker Protection Standard (WPS); OSHA 29 CFR 1928.110; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: rei_hours
attributes.description: The Restricted Entry Interval (REI) duration in hours applicable to the planned agrochemical product for this spray window. Defines the minimum time workers must stay out of treated areas after application. Sourced from the product label and EPA registration.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170 Worker Protection Standard; FIFRA Label Requirements

attributes.name: sensitive_area_proximity_m
attributes.description: Distance in metres from the field boundary to the nearest sensitive area (water body, school, residential zone, organic buffer zone). Used to apply appropriate buffer zone restrictions and drift management requirements.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170; EPA Drift Reduction Technology; USDA NRCS BMP; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: solar_radiation_mj_m2
attributes.description: Solar radiation in megajoules per square metre during the spray window period. High solar radiation increases volatilisation risk for certain herbicides and affects photodegradation rates of active ingredients.
attributes.references: Climate FieldView; GRDC Spray Decision Guidelines; EPA FIFRA

attributes.name: state_drift_constraint
attributes.description: Indicates whether state-level pesticide drift regulations impose additional constraints on this spray window beyond federal EPA requirements. State regulations may be more restrictive than federal standards.
attributes.references: State Pesticide Regulatory Agencies; EPA FIFRA Section 24(a); USDA APHIS

attributes.name: temp_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum air temperature in degrees Celsius during the spray window period. High temperatures increase volatilisation and drift risk; many labels specify maximum temperature limits for application.
attributes.references: EPA FIFRA Label Requirements; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; Trimble Ag Software

attributes.name: temp_min_c
attributes.description: Minimum air temperature in degrees Celsius during the spray window period. Temperature thresholds affect pesticide efficacy, volatilisation risk, and label compliance for temperature-sensitive products.
attributes.references: EPA FIFRA Label Requirements; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; Trimble Ag Software

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this spray window record was last modified. Tracks recalculations triggered by updated forecast data or manual overrides. Supports audit trail and data quality monitoring.
attributes.references: FSMA §112; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; ISO 22000; SOX Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: wind_direction_deg
attributes.description: Prevailing wind direction in degrees (0–360, meteorological convention) during the spray window. Used to assess drift trajectory relative to sensitive areas, water bodies, and neighbouring fields.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170 Drift Reduction; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: wind_speed_max_kmh
attributes.description: Maximum observed or forecast wind speed in kilometres per hour during the spray window period. Exceeding label-specified maximum wind speed thresholds triggers window closure to prevent off-target drift.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170; USDA NRCS BMP; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: wind_speed_min_kmh
attributes.description: Minimum observed or forecast wind speed in kilometres per hour during the spray window period. Used to assess drift risk and label compliance; most pesticide labels require a minimum wind speed to ensure adequate air movement.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170; USDA NRCS BMP; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: window_duration_min
attributes.description: Calculated duration of the spray window in minutes, derived from window_start and window_end. Stored for operational scheduling and equipment dispatch planning without requiring runtime calculation.
attributes.references: Climate FieldView; Trimble Ag Software Spray Planning

attributes.name: window_end
attributes.description: The datetime marking the close of the meteorologically permissible application window. Spray operations must cease by this time to remain within label-compliant and regulatory-compliant conditions.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; Climate FieldView Spray Window Logic

attributes.name: window_reference_code
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this spray window record, used in crop protection planning workflows, application scheduling, and audit documentation. Format: SW- followed by alphanumeric characters.
attributes.references: EPA Label Compliance; FSMA §112; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: window_source
attributes.description: Indicates whether this spray window was calculated from forecast weather data, actual observed data, manually entered conditions, or a blended model output. Affects confidence level and audit trail for regulatory documentation.
attributes.references: Climate FieldView; DTN Weather Feed; Trimble Ag Software

attributes.name: window_start
attributes.description: The principal business event timestamp marking the beginning of the meteorologically permissible application window. Represents the earliest datetime at which spray operations may commence under current conditions.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; Climate FieldView Spray Window Logic

attributes.name: window_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the spray window record. 'open' indicates meteorological conditions are permissible for application; 'closed' indicates conditions are not met; 'pending' indicates evaluation in progress; 'expired' indicates the window datetime has passed; 'cancelled' indicates the window was voided.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 170 (Worker Protection Standard); GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6

attributes.name: window_type
attributes.description: Classification of the agrochemical application type for which this spray window is calculated. Determines applicable regulatory constraints, label requirements, and drift risk thresholds. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pesticide|herbicide|fungicide|insecticide|fertilizer|growth_regulator|adjuvant|micronutrient — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA FIFRA Label Requirements; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 7.6; USDA NRCS BMP

products.name: planting_window
products.description: Calculated time window record identifying optimal periods for field planting operations based on soil temperature thresholds, soil moisture levels, air temperature forecasts, and precipitation outlook. Stores window start/end dates, soil temperature at 2-inch and 4-inch depth, field trafficability score, frost risk probability, GDD accumulation outlook, and recommended crop types for the window.
products.reference: Climate FieldView Planting Window / USDA Planting Date Guidelines

attributes.name: planting_window_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the planting window record.
attributes.references: Internal Data Standard

attributes.name: crop_enterprise_budget_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.crop_enterprise_budget. Business justification: Approved planting windows determine the crop calendar that anchors enterprise budget revenue recognition timing and planting cost scheduling. Budget planners use final planting dates from planting win

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: Reference to the agricultural field for which this planting window is calculated. Links to the field master record containing geographic boundaries, soil type, and historical yield data.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; Esri ArcGIS

attributes.name: forecast_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.forecast. Business justification: Planting windows are calculated using weather forecast data (temperature forecasts, precipitation probability, ET forecast, GDD outlook). Linking planting_window to the specific forecast record used d
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: growing_season_id
attributes.description: Reference to the growing season within which this planting window falls, enabling seasonal aggregation and year-over-year comparison of planting window analytics.
attributes.references: Granular Farm Management; SAP S/4HANA PP module

attributes.name: seed_variety_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.seed_variety. Business justification: Planting window suitability assessments are variety-specific — soil_temp thresholds, GDD outlook, and frost_risk_probability must be evaluated against the seed variety's recommended_planting_regions,
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: soil_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to land.soil_profile. Business justification: Planting window calculations depend on soil drainage class, texture, and bulk density to assess trafficability and soil warming rates. Linking planting_window to land.soil_profile allows agronomists t
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: soil_temperature_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.soil_temperature. Business justification: Planting window calculations are critically dependent on soil temperature (minimum soil temp thresholds for germination vary by crop). planting_window has soil_temp_2in_c and soil_temp_4in_c — these a
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary weather station providing meteorological data inputs for this planting window calculation, including temperature, precipitation, and evapotranspiration (ET) readings.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feeds; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.weather_zone. Business justification: Planting windows are calculated for geographic zones as well as individual fields. planting_window has geographic_zone_code (STRING) which is a denormalized reference to weather_zone.zone_code. Adding
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: agronomist_approved
attributes.description: Indicates whether a certified agronomist has reviewed and approved this planting window recommendation before it is used for operational planting decisions. Required for compliance with GLOBALG.A.P. and internal Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) protocols.
attributes.references: GLOBALG.A.P. Control Points; USDA GAP Certification

attributes.name: air_temp_max_forecast_c
attributes.description: Forecast maximum air temperature in degrees Celsius for the planting window period. Used to assess heat stress risk and optimal growing degree day (GDD) accumulation potential during early crop establishment.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feeds; NOAA National Weather Service

attributes.name: air_temp_min_forecast_c
attributes.description: Forecast minimum air temperature in degrees Celsius for the planting window period. Used to assess frost risk and cold stress potential for newly planted seeds and emerging seedlings.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feeds; NOAA National Weather Service

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the agronomist or authorized user approved this planting window record for operational use. Null if agronomist_approved is False.
attributes.references: GLOBALG.A.P.; Internal SOPs

attributes.name: calculated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this planting window record was first calculated and created in the system. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for the planting window lifecycle.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance; FSMA Traceability Rule

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: Method used to derive the planting window. Algorithmic uses rule-based thresholds; model_based uses predictive weather models; manual indicates agronomist override; hybrid combines automated calculation with manual adjustment.
attributes.references: Trimble Ag Software; Climate FieldView; Internal FMIS Standards

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: Qualitative confidence level of the planting window calculation based on the reliability of input weather forecast data and soil sensor readings. High confidence indicates short-range forecasts with high-quality sensor data; low confidence indicates extended-range forecasts or missing sensor inputs.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feeds; Climate FieldView; NOAA Forecast Confidence Standards

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Primary data source system used to generate the planting window calculation. Identifies the originating system for data lineage, quality auditing, and source reconciliation purposes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: climate_fieldview|dtn|noaa|iot_sensor|trimble|manual|granular — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance; FSMA Traceability Rule

attributes.name: et_forecast_mm
attributes.description: Forecast evapotranspiration (ET) in millimeters for the planting window period, representing estimated water loss from soil evaporation and plant transpiration. Used for irrigation scheduling and water balance calculations during early crop establishment.
attributes.references: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET Standard; Climate FieldView; USDA NRCS

attributes.name: field_area_ha
attributes.description: Total plantable area of the field in hectares applicable to this planting window. Used for seed quantity calculations, equipment scheduling, and labor resource planning.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS; John Deere Operations Center; ISO 19152 Land Administration

attributes.name: final_planting_date
attributes.description: The USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) designated final planting date for the primary crop type in this geographic area. Planting after this date may result in reduced crop insurance coverage or late-planting payment reductions.
attributes.references: USDA RMA Final Planting Date Schedule; FCIC

attributes.name: forecast_horizon_days
attributes.description: Number of days ahead from the calculation timestamp that the weather forecast data covers. Shorter horizons (1–7 days) yield higher confidence planting windows; longer horizons (8–14+ days) are used for preliminary planning.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feeds; NOAA National Weather Service

attributes.name: frost_risk_probability_pct
attributes.description: Estimated probability (0–100%) of a frost event occurring during the planting window period. Derived from forecast minimum temperatures and historical climatological data. High frost risk may delay planting of frost-sensitive crops.
attributes.references: NOAA Climate Data; DTN Weather Feeds; USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA)

attributes.name: gdd_base_temp_c
attributes.description: Base temperature in degrees Celsius used in the Growing Degree Day (GDD) calculation for this planting window. Varies by crop type (e.g., 10°C for corn, 7.2°C for wheat). Ensures GDD outlook values are crop-specific and agronomically meaningful.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS GDD Calculation Standards; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: gdd_outlook
attributes.description: Forecast accumulated Growing Degree Days (GDD) expected during the planting window period, calculated using the standard base temperature method. Supports crop maturity scheduling and hybrid/variety selection decisions.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS GDD Calculation Standards; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: insurance_relevant
attributes.description: Indicates whether this planting window record is relevant for crop insurance documentation purposes, such as establishing the planted-within-final-planting-date compliance required by USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) crop insurance policies.
attributes.references: USDA RMA Crop Insurance; FCIC Final Planting Date Standards

attributes.name: irrigation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether supplemental irrigation is recommended prior to or during the planting window to achieve adequate soil moisture for seed germination. Derived from soil moisture levels and evapotranspiration (ET) forecast.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Irrigation Water Management; FAO-56

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for agronomist or field manager observations, special conditions, or operational notes associated with this planting window, such as localized drainage issues, equipment availability constraints, or crop variety-specific considerations.
attributes.references: Internal FMIS Standards; Granular Farm Management

attributes.name: precip_forecast_mm
attributes.description: Total forecast precipitation in millimeters expected during the planting window period. Excessive precipitation may delay planting operations and increase disease pressure; insufficient precipitation may require supplemental irrigation scheduling.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feeds; WASDE Report; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: precip_probability_pct
attributes.description: Forecast probability of precipitation occurrence (0–100%) during the planting window period. Used in conjunction with precipitation amount forecast to assess planting operation scheduling risk.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Feeds; NOAA National Weather Service

attributes.name: recommended_crop_types
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of crop types agronomically recommended for planting during this window based on soil temperature, moisture, and forecast conditions (e.g., 'corn,soybean,wheat'). Supports crop planning and seed procurement decisions.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Crop Planting Date Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: soil_moisture_pct
attributes.description: Volumetric soil moisture content expressed as a percentage at the time of window calculation. Used to assess field trafficability and seed-to-soil contact conditions. Values above field capacity indicate risk of compaction and poor germination.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; ISO 11461 Soil Moisture Measurement

attributes.name: soil_temp_2in_c
attributes.description: Measured or forecast soil temperature at 2-inch (5 cm) depth in degrees Celsius at the time of window calculation. Critical threshold indicator for seed germination viability, particularly for corn (minimum 10°C) and soybean (minimum 12°C).
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Soil Temperature Standards; Climate FieldView IoT Sensors

attributes.name: soil_temp_4in_c
attributes.description: Measured or forecast soil temperature at 4-inch (10 cm) depth in degrees Celsius at the time of window calculation. Provides a more stable and agronomically representative temperature reading for seed placement depth decisions.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Soil Temperature Standards; Climate FieldView IoT Sensors

attributes.name: spray_window_open

attributes.name: noaa_climate_division
attributes.description: NOAA-assigned climate division code (state + division number, e.g., 'IL01') used to aggregate station data to regional climate normals. Supports WASDE regional yield estimation and USDA crop reporting district alignment.
attributes.references: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI) Climate Division Dataset; USDA WASDE

attributes.name: normal_period_end_year
attributes.description: The last calendar year of the 30-year baseline period used to compute this climate normal (e.g., 2020 for the 1991-2020 WMO normal period).
attributes.references: World Meteorological Organization (WMO) Technical Regulations No. 49; NOAA 1991-2020 U.S. Climate Normals

attributes.name: normal_period_start_year
attributes.description: The first calendar year of the 30-year baseline period used to compute this climate normal (e.g., 1991 for the 1991-2020 WMO normal period).
attributes.references: World Meteorological Organization (WMO) Technical Regulations No. 49; NOAA 1991-2020 U.S. Climate Normals

attributes.name: normal_status
attributes.description: Lifecycle status of this climate normal record. Active records are used for operational decisions; superseded records are retained for historical comparison and crop insurance documentation.
attributes.references: NOAA Climate Normals Program; USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) crop insurance documentation

attributes.name: normal_type
attributes.description: Temporal granularity of this climate normal record — monthly (one record per calendar month), seasonal (DJF/MAM/JJA/SON), or annual (full-year aggregate).
attributes.references: WMO Guidelines on the Calculation of Climate Normals (WMO-No. 1203)

attributes.name: precip_days_normal
attributes.description: 30-year average number of days with measurable precipitation (≥0.25 mm) for the applicable month or season. Used for spray window planning and field operation scheduling.
attributes.references: WMO Climate Normals (WMO-No. 1203); IPM spray window guidelines; EPA pesticide application regulations

attributes.name: precip_normal_mm
attributes.description: 30-year average total precipitation in millimetres for the applicable month or season. Baseline for irrigation scheduling, water resource planning, and crop insurance actuarial calculations.
attributes.references: WMO Climate Normals (WMO-No. 1203); USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA); FSMA water use compliance

attributes.name: published_date
attributes.description: Date on which this climate normal record was officially published or made available for operational use. Used for version control and regulatory audit trails under FSMA and crop insurance documentation requirements.
attributes.references: NOAA NCEI Climate Normals Publication; USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA); FSMA compliance

attributes.name: quality_flag
attributes.description: Quality control status of the climate normal record indicating whether the underlying 30-year observation series passed automated QC checks, was estimated via interpolation, or contains missing data gaps.
attributes.references: NOAA NCEI Quality Control Procedures; WMO Data Quality Management Framework; ISO 22000 data integrity

attributes.name: season_code
attributes.description: WMO meteorological season code: DJF (December-January-February / Winter), MAM (March-April-May / Spring), JJA (June-July-August / Summer), SON (September-October-November / Autumn). Null for monthly or annual normal_type records.
attributes.references: WMO Guidelines on the Calculation of Climate Normals (WMO-No. 1203)

attributes.name: snowfall_normal_mm
attributes.description: 30-year average total snowfall expressed as water equivalent in millimetres for the applicable month or season. Relevant for soil moisture recharge estimation and spring planting window forecasting.
attributes.references: NOAA Climate Normals; USDA NRCS Snow Survey and Water Supply Forecasting

attributes.name: solar_radiation_normal_mj_m2
attributes.description: 30-year average incoming solar radiation in megajoules per square metre per day for the applicable month or season. Required input for FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET calculations and NDVI baseline modelling.
attributes.references: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith; NDVI remote sensing standards; WMO Climate Normals

attributes.name: temp_max_c
attributes.description: 30-year average of daily maximum temperatures in degrees Celsius for the applicable month or season. Used for heat stress thresholds and GDD upper-cap calculations.
attributes.references: WMO Climate Normals (WMO-No. 1203); USDA NASS crop progress reports

attributes.name: temp_mean_c
attributes.description: 30-year average mean daily temperature in degrees Celsius for the applicable month or season. Core input for GDD accumulation norms and WASDE yield estimation.
attributes.references: WMO Climate Normals (WMO-No. 1203); USDA WASDE; FAO-56

attributes.name: temp_min_c
attributes.description: 30-year average of daily minimum temperatures in degrees Celsius for the applicable month or season. Critical for frost risk assessment and crop variety selection.
attributes.references: WMO Climate Normals (WMO-No. 1203); USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this climate normal record in the data lakehouse. Tracks revisions from reprocessing, QC corrections, or source data updates.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 data integrity controls; NOAA NCEI data revision policies

attributes.name: wind_speed_normal_ms
attributes.description: 30-year average wind speed in metres per second at 2-metre height for the applicable month or season. Used in ET calculations, spray window assessments, and pesticide drift risk modelling per EPA REI guidelines.
attributes.references: FAO-56; EPA pesticide application wind speed limits; WMO Climate Normals

attributes.name: wmo_station_number
attributes.description: Official WMO 5- or 6-digit station identifier assigned by the World Meteorological Organization. Enables cross-referencing with NOAA NCEI, DTN, and international climate databases for data lineage and audit.
attributes.references: WMO Integrated Global Observing System (WIGOS); NOAA NCEI Station Catalogue

attributes.name: years_of_record
attributes.description: Actual number of years of valid observational data used to compute this normal (may be less than 30 if data gaps exist). Values below 25 indicate reduced statistical confidence per WMO guidelines.
attributes.references: WMO Guidelines on the Calculation of Climate Normals (WMO-No. 1203)

products.name: irrigation_schedule
products.description: Weather-driven irrigation scheduling record generated from ET calculations, soil moisture readings, and precipitation forecasts for a specific field or irrigation zone. Stores scheduled irrigation date/time, recommended application volume (acre-inches), irrigation method (drip, pivot, flood), ET deficit being addressed, soil moisture target, and precipitation credit applied. Integrates with John Deere Operations Center and Trimble Ag VRA irrigation prescriptions.
products.reference: FAO Irrigation Scheduling / USDA NRCS Irrigation Water Management

attributes.name: irrigation_schedule_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the irrigation schedule record. Primary key for the irrigation_schedule data product in the weather domain Silver layer.
attributes.references: Internal Data Architecture Standard

attributes.name: crew_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.crew. Business justification: Irrigation schedules are executed by specific irrigation crews. Linking irrigation_schedule to crew enables labor cost allocation, crew utilization reporting, and ensures the right crew is dispatched
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: crop_enterprise_budget_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.crop_enterprise_budget. Business justification: Irrigation schedules drive water and energy costs that are major line items in crop enterprise budgets. Linking irrigation schedules to the enterprise budget enables actual vs planned irrigation cost
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: drought_index_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.drought_index. Business justification: Irrigation scheduling is directly driven by drought conditions — drought_index has irrigation_recommended and irrigation_deficit_mm fields that feed directly into irrigation schedule generation. Linki
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: evapotranspiration_id
attributes.description: Reference to the evapotranspiration calculation record that drove this irrigation schedule recommendation. Links to the weather.evapotranspiration product.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; USDA NRCS Irrigation Water Management

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: Reference to the agricultural field or irrigation zone for which this irrigation schedule was generated. Links to the field master record in the crop management domain.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center Field Mapping; Trimble Ag Software Field Planning

attributes.name: forecast_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.forecast. Business justification: Irrigation schedules are generated using weather forecast data (precipitation probability, ET forecast). Linking irrigation_schedule to the specific forecast record used during schedule generation pro
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: irrigation_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to land.irrigation_zone. Business justification: Every irrigation schedule applies to a specific physical irrigation zone. Replacing the denormalized irrigation_zone_code text with a proper FK to land.irrigation_zone enables water volume tracking ag
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: soil_temperature_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.soil_temperature. Business justification: Irrigation scheduling decisions are influenced by soil temperature (cold soils reduce crop water uptake, affecting irrigation requirements). Linking irrigation_schedule to the specific soil_temperatur
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: application_rate_mm_hr
attributes.description: The rate at which water is applied during the irrigation event, expressed in millimeters per hour. Determines irrigation duration and must not exceed soil infiltration rate to prevent runoff.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; EPA Best Management Practices (BMP)

attributes.name: application_volume_acre_in
attributes.description: The recommended volume of water to be applied during this irrigation event, expressed in acre-inches. Derived from the ET deficit calculation and soil moisture target. Standard unit for US agricultural irrigation scheduling.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: application_volume_mm
attributes.description: The recommended volume of water to be applied during this irrigation event, expressed in millimeters depth equivalent. Metric unit for international reporting and FAO-aligned ET calculations.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; ISO 14001; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the agronomist, farm manager, or operator who approved this irrigation schedule for execution. Supports audit trail and accountability requirements under GLOBALG.A.P. and FSMA.
attributes.references: GLOBALG.A.P.; FSMA; USDA GAP (Good Agricultural Practices)

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this irrigation schedule was approved for execution. Part of the schedule lifecycle audit trail required for GLOBALG.A.P. and FSMA compliance documentation.
attributes.references: GLOBALG.A.P.; FSMA; USDA GAP (Good Agricultural Practices)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this irrigation schedule record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 22000; FSMA; Internal Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: crop_coefficient
attributes.description: The dimensionless crop coefficient (Kc) used to convert reference ET (ETo) to crop-specific ET (ETc). Varies by crop type and growth stage per FAO-56 methodology. Critical input to the ET deficit calculation.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; USDA NRCS

attributes.name: crop_growth_stage
attributes.description: The current phenological growth stage of the crop at the time of scheduling (e.g., V6, R1, R3 for corn; vegetative, flowering, pod fill for soybeans). Influences crop coefficient and irrigation priority.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: crop_type
attributes.description: The type of crop being irrigated (e.g., corn, soybeans, wheat, cotton). Determines crop coefficient (Kc) used in ET calculations and influences soil moisture targets and irrigation timing.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: estimated_duration_min
attributes.description: The estimated duration of the irrigation event in minutes, calculated from the recommended application volume and application rate. Used for equipment scheduling and energy cost estimation.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; Trimble Ag Software

attributes.name: estimated_water_volume_m3
attributes.description: The total estimated volume of water to be applied during this irrigation event, expressed in cubic meters. Used for water use reporting, permit compliance, and cost accounting.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Water Act; USDA NRCS; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

attributes.name: et_deficit_mm
attributes.description: The cumulative soil water deficit being addressed by this irrigation event, calculated as the difference between crop ET demand and effective precipitation received. Expressed in millimeters. Core driver of the irrigation recommendation.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: external_schedule_ref
attributes.description: The reference identifier from the originating external system (e.g., John Deere Operations Center task ID, Trimble Ag prescription ID, Climate FieldView recommendation ID). Enables bidirectional traceability to source systems.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; Trimble Ag Software; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: frost_protection_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this irrigation event is scheduled for frost/freeze protection purposes rather than crop water demand. When True, the schedule is triggered by frost alert conditions rather than ET deficit.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; weather.frost_alert; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: generation_source
attributes.description: The system or data source that generated this irrigation schedule recommendation. Supports data lineage, audit, and integration traceability across Climate FieldView, Trimble Ag, John Deere Operations Center, and IoT sensor networks. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: climate_fieldview|trimble_ag|john_deere_ops|granular|manual|iot_sensor|dtn_feed — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Climate FieldView; Trimble Ag Software; John Deere Operations Center; DTN

attributes.name: irrigation_method
attributes.description: The physical method of water application for this scheduled irrigation event. Determines application efficiency, equipment requirements, and water use calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: drip|center_pivot|flood|sprinkler|subsurface_drip|furrow|lateral_move|micro_sprinkler — promote to reference product if additional methods are needed]
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Irrigation Water Management; EPA WaterSense; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: phi_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this irrigation schedule has been reviewed for compliance with Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) requirements for any recently applied agrochemicals. Relevant for food safety and MRL compliance.
attributes.references: EPA PHI Regulations; FDA FSMA Produce Safety Rule; GLOBALG.A.P.; MRL Standards

attributes.name: precip_credit_mm
attributes.description: The effective precipitation credit applied to reduce the irrigation requirement, accounting for forecast precipitation probability and soil infiltration capacity. Expressed in millimeters.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Effective Precipitation; FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56

attributes.name: precip_forecast_mm
attributes.description: The forecasted precipitation amount in millimeters for the scheduling window, sourced from DTN weather feeds or Climate FieldView. Used to calculate precipitation credit and adjust the recommended application volume.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Services; Climate FieldView; NOAA National Weather Service

attributes.name: precip_probability_pct
attributes.description: The probability of precipitation occurring during the scheduled irrigation window, expressed as a percentage. Used to determine whether to proceed with irrigation or defer pending rainfall.
attributes.references: DTN Weather Services; NOAA National Weather Service; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: schedule_notes
attributes.description: Free-text operational notes entered by the agronomist or farm manager regarding this irrigation schedule, such as equipment constraints, field access issues, or special instructions for the irrigation operator.
attributes.references: Granular Farm Management; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: schedule_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the irrigation schedule, used in operational communications, FMIS records, and integration with John Deere Operations Center and Trimble Ag. Format: IRSCHED-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; Trimble Ag Software; FMIS Standards

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the irrigation schedule. 'draft' indicates pending review; 'scheduled' indicates approved and queued; 'in_progress' indicates irrigation is actively running; 'completed' indicates finished; 'cancelled' indicates voided before execution; 'skipped' indicates bypassed due to precipitation or other conditions.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; Granular Farm Management

attributes.name: schedule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the method used to generate this irrigation schedule. 'et_based' uses evapotranspiration deficit calculations; 'soil_moisture_based' uses sensor readings; 'calendar_based' uses fixed intervals; 'forecast_based' uses precipitation forecast adjustments; 'manual' is operator-entered.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Irrigation Water Management; FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56

attributes.name: scheduled_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which irrigation is scheduled to occur. Used for operational planning, spray window coordination, and crop insurance documentation.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; FSMA Produce Safety Rule; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: scheduled_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The projected date and time at which irrigation is scheduled to complete. Used for equipment scheduling, labor planning, and energy cost estimation.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; Granular Farm Management

attributes.name: scheduled_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time at which irrigation is scheduled to begin. Critical for pivot and drip system automation, labor scheduling, and integration with John Deere Operations Center equipment dispatch.
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center; Trimble Ag Software

attributes.name: soil_moisture_current_pct
attributes.description: The measured or estimated current volumetric soil moisture content at the time the schedule was generated, expressed as a percentage of field capacity. Sourced from IoT field sensors or modeled estimates.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Soil Moisture Monitoring; IoT Sensor Standards; Climate FieldView

attributes.name: soil_moisture_target_pct
attributes.description: The target volumetric soil moisture content to be achieved after irrigation, expressed as a percentage of field capacity. Defined by crop type, growth stage, and soil type. Used to calculate required application volume.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS; FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; GLOBALG.A.P.

attributes.name: spray_window_conflict
attributes.description: Indicates whether this irrigation schedule conflicts with an active pesticide or fertilizer spray window. When True, irrigation timing may need to be adjusted to avoid diluting chemical applications or violating Restricted Entry Interval (REI) requirements.
attributes.references: EPA REI Regulations; USDA APHIS; GLOBALG.A.P.; FSMA

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this irrigation schedule record was last modified. Tracks revisions to the schedule including volume adjustments, timing changes, or status updates.
attributes.references: ISO 22000; FSMA; Internal Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: water_source
attributes.description: The source of water used for this irrigation event. Relevant for water rights compliance, cost accounting, and environmental reporting under EPA and state water authority regulations.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Water Act; USDA NRCS; State Water Rights Regulations; ISO 14001

attributes.name: water_stress_index
attributes.description: A dimensionless index (0.0 to 1.0) quantifying the degree of crop water stress at the time of scheduling. A value of 0 indicates no stress; 1.0 indicates maximum stress. Used to prioritize irrigation scheduling across multiple fields.
attributes.references: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView

products.name: alert
products.description: Official weather alert, warning, and frost/freeze advisory record issued by NWS, DTN, or internal farm management systems for a weather zone or field. Stores alert type (tornado, severe thunderstorm, flash flood, heat advisory, winter storm, high wind, frost/freeze advisory, wildfire smoke), alert severity (advisory/watch/warning/emergency), issuance and expiration datetime, affected geographic zone, predicted low temperature for frost events, frost probability, crop-specific vulnerability rating, recommended protective actions (including frost cloth, irrigation frost protection), alert source, and acknowledgment status. SSOT for all weather alert types including frost/freeze events, consolidating all alert lifecycle management in a single product.
products.reference: NWS Weather Alert Classification / CAP (Common Alerting Protocol)

attributes.name: alert_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each weather alert record. Primary key for the weather_alert data product in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Internal Data Architecture Standard

attributes.name: crew_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.crew. Business justification: Severe weather alerts (lightning, high wind, hail) trigger mandatory crew evacuation and work-stoppage protocols under OSHA and WPS. Safety managers must know which crew is in the affected area to exe
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: delivery_location_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.delivery_location. Business justification: Weather alerts (blizzards, tornadoes, ice storms) directly affect specific customer receiving facilities. Agriculture logistics teams associate weather alerts with impacted delivery locations to trigg
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific agricultural field affected by this weather alert. Enables field-level alert routing, crop vulnerability assessment, and precision protective action recommendations within the Farm Management Information System (FMIS).
attributes.references: John Deere Operations Center Field Mapping; Trimble Ag Software Field Planning; Esri ArcGIS GIS Integration

attributes.name: station_id
attributes.description: Reference to the weather observation station associated with this alert. Links to the station providing the meteorological data underpinning the alert, sourced from IoT field sensors or DTN weather network stations.
attributes.references: NOAA Station Identification Standard; DTN Weather Station Network; IoT Sensor Integration

attributes.name: zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to weather.weather_zone. Business justification: Official NWS weather alerts are issued by geographic zone (NWS zone-based alert system). weather_alert has geographic_zone_code (STRING) which is a denormalized reference to weather_zone.zone_code. Ad
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: acknowledged_by
attributes.description: Name or system identifier of the farm manager, agronomist, or operator who acknowledged this weather alert. Required for FSMA compliance audit trails and GLOBALG.A.P. certification documentation demonstrating that alerts were acted upon by responsible personnel.
attributes.references: FSMA Produce Safety Rule; GLOBALG.A.P. Responsible Person Requirements; ISO 22000 Clause 5.3

attributes.name: acknowledgement_timestamp
attributes.description: The datetime when the weather alert was acknowledged by a responsible farm manager or operator. Supports audit trail requirements for FSMA compliance, GLOBALG.A.P. certification, and internal Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) adherence.
attributes.references: FSMA Produce Safety Rule Recordkeeping; GLOBALG.A.P. Audit Trail Requirements; ISO 22000 Food Safety Management

attributes.name: affected_area_ha
attributes.description: Total agricultural land area affected by this weather alert, expressed in hectares. Used for crop insurance documentation, loss estimation, and resource allocation for protective actions. Supports USDA crop insurance claim substantiation.
attributes.references: USDA Crop Insurance Program; FSMA Produce Safety Rule; GLOBALG.A.P. Risk Assessment

attributes.name: alert_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the weather alert, typically assigned by the issuing authority (e.g., NWS event number, DTN alert code, or internal farm management system reference). Used for cross-system traceability and regulatory documentation.
attributes.references: National Weather Service (NWS) Alert Numbering Standard; DTN Weather Services

attributes.name: alert_source
attributes.description: Originating system or authority that issued the weather alert. Identifies whether the alert originated from the National Weather Service (NWS), DTN Data Transmission Network weather feed, Climate FieldView platform, internal Farm Management Information System (FMIS), NOAA, or a state agricultural agency.
attributes.references: DTN AgWeather Services; NWS Public Alert Feed; Climate FieldView API; USDA FMIS Integration Standards

attributes.name: alert_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the weather alert record. Tracks whether the alert is newly issued, currently active, has been updated with revised information, cancelled by the issuing authority, or has naturally expired past its valid period.
attributes.references: NWS Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) v1.2; OASIS CAP Standard

attributes.name: alert_type
attributes.description: Classification of the meteorological hazard represented by this alert. Identifies the specific weather phenomenon such as tornado, severe thunderstorm, flash flood, heat advisory, winter storm, high wind, frost/freeze advisory, or wildfire smoke. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tornado|severe_thunderstorm|flash_flood|heat_advisory|winter_storm|high_wind|frost_freeze|wildfire_smoke|drought|hail|dense_fog|excessive_heat — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NWS Weather Event Types; NOAA Hazardous Weather Terminology; DTN AgWeather Alert Classification

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording when this weather alert record was first created in the Databricks Silver Layer data product. Distinct from the issued_timestamp (business event time). Supports data lineage, FSMA recordkeeping compliance, and SOX audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: FSMA Recordkeeping Requirements; SOX Section 404 Audit Trail; ISO 22000 Clause 8.5.1

attributes.name: critical_threshold_temp_c
attributes.description: The temperature threshold in degrees Celsius below which crop damage is expected for the affected crop type and growth stage. Used to determine alert severity and trigger protective action recommendations. Varies by crop species and phenological stage.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Crop Freeze Damage Thresholds; GLOBALG.A.P. Crop Protection Standards; University Extension Frost Damage Guidelines

attributes.name: crop_growth_stage
attributes.description: The phenological growth stage of the affected crop at the time of the alert (e.g., germination, emergence, vegetative, flowering, grain fill, maturity). Growth stage critically determines crop vulnerability to weather hazards and informs protective action urgency.
attributes.references: BBCH Scale (Biologische Bundesanstalt, Bundessortenamt und CHemische Industrie); USDA NRCS Crop Growth Stage Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P. Crop Protection

attributes.name: crop_type
attributes.description: The primary crop type affected by this weather alert (e.g., corn, soybeans, wheat, cotton, specialty crops). Used to determine crop-specific vulnerability ratings, damage thresholds, and recommended protective actions. Aligns with USDA crop classification codes.
attributes.references: USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) Crop Classification; GLOBALG.A.P. Crop Registry

attributes.name: crop_vulnerability_rating
attributes.description: Assessed vulnerability rating of the affected crop to the specific weather hazard at its current growth stage. Drives prioritization of protective actions and resource allocation. Ratings range from low (minimal expected damage) to critical (severe or total crop loss expected).
attributes.references: USDA Crop Insurance Actuarial Standards; GLOBALG.A.P. Risk Assessment Framework; University Extension Crop Vulnerability Guidelines

attributes.name: dew_point_temp_c
attributes.description: Forecast or observed dew point temperature in degrees Celsius. Critical for frost event characterization — when dew point is below 0°C, frost deposition is expected. Also used for spray window assessment and disease pressure modeling.
attributes.references: WMO Dew Point Calculation Standard; NOAA Frost Prediction Methodology; EPA Pesticide Application Guidelines

attributes.name: end_timestamp
attributes.description: The datetime when the weather alert expires and hazardous conditions are expected to cease. Determines the window during which protective actions must remain in place. Used for irrigation frost protection scheduling and spray window re-opening decisions.
attributes.references: NWS CAP v1.2 expires element; GLOBALG.A.P. Integrated Pest Management (IPM) scheduling

attributes.name: estimated_crop_loss_pct
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of crop yield loss expected if no protective action is taken, based on forecast conditions, crop type, and growth stage. Used for crop insurance pre-loss documentation, financial risk assessment, and USDA WASDE reporting inputs.
attributes.references: USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) Crop Insurance Loss Assessment; WASDE Report Methodology; GLOBALG.A.P. Loss Documentation

attributes.name: external_alert_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier from the external source system (DTN, Climate FieldView, or state agency) that originated this alert record. Supports data lineage, deduplication, and reconciliation with upstream weather data providers.
attributes.references: DTN AgWeather API Reference; Climate FieldView Data Integration Standard; USDA Data Interoperability Guidelines

attributes.name: forecast_low_temp_c
attributes.description: Predicted minimum temperature in degrees Celsius for the alert period. Critical for frost/freeze advisory events to assess crop damage risk, determine Growing Degree Day (GDD) impact, and trigger irrigation frost protection systems.
attributes.references: NWS Temperature Forecast Standard; USDA NRCS Frost Depth Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P. Crop Protection

attributes.name: frost_probability_pct
attributes.description: Statistical probability (0-100%) that frost conditions will occur during the alert period, as calculated by the issuing weather service. Used for risk-based decision-making on protective action deployment and crop insurance pre-loss documentation.
attributes.references: NWS Probabilistic Forecast Standards; DTN AgWeather Frost Probability Model; USDA Crop Insurance Actuarial Standards

attributes.name: frost_type
attributes.description: Classification of the frost mechanism expected during the alert event. Radiation frost occurs on clear calm nights; advection frost results from cold air mass movement; evaporation frost occurs with rapid moisture loss; freeze indicates temperatures below 0°C causing ice crystal formation in plant tissue.
attributes.references: NOAA Frost Classification Standard; USDA NRCS Frost Type Definitions; University Extension Frost Management Guidelines

attributes.name: gdd_impact_estimate
attributes.description: Estimated impact on Growing Degree Day (GDD) accumulation resulting from the weather event described in this alert. Negative values indicate GDD loss due to frost or extreme cold; used to recalculate predicted crop maturity dates and adjust harvest scheduling.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Growing Degree Day Methodology; Climate FieldView GDD Analytics; GLOBALG.A.P. Crop Development Tracking

attributes.name: insurance_claim_relevant
attributes.description: Indicates whether this weather alert event is relevant for crop insurance claim documentation under USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) programs. When True, the alert record is preserved as supporting evidence for potential indemnity claims.
attributes.references: USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) Crop Insurance Program; FSMA Recordkeeping Requirements; GLOBALG.A.P. Documentation Standards

attributes.name: irrigation_frost_protection
attributes.description: Indicates whether overhead irrigation frost protection has been recommended or activated in response to this frost/freeze alert. Irrigation frost protection uses latent heat of freezing water to protect crops from freeze damage. Integrates with irrigation scheduling systems.
attributes.references: USDA NRCS Irrigation Frost Protection Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P. Water Resource Management; Irrigation Association Best Practices

attributes.name: issued_timestamp
attributes.description: The principal real-world event timestamp when the weather alert was officially issued by the originating authority. Represents the business event time distinct from the record audit timestamp. attributes.name: latitude

attributes.references: WGS84 Coordinate Reference System; Esri ArcGIS Spatial Standard; GPS/RTK Positioning Standard

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the alert centroid or point of origin in decimal degrees (WGS84). Used in conjunction with latitude for GIS spatial analysis, field boundary intersection, and precision agriculture alert targeting.
attributes.references: WGS84 Coordinate Reference System; Esri ArcGIS Spatial Standard; GPS/RTK Positioning Standard

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, observations, or context related to this weather alert. May include agronomist commentary, field-specific conditions, or supplementary guidance not captured in structured fields. Supports GLOBALG.A.P. documentation requirements.
attributes.references: GLOBALG.A.P. Documentation Standards; USDA GAP/GMP Recordkeeping Guidelines

attributes.name: nws_event_code

attributes.references: NWS Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) v1.2; NOAA Weather Event Database; USDA Crop Insurance Documentation Requirements

attributes.name: recommended_action
attributes.description: Prescribed protective action recommended in response to this weather alert, such as deploy frost cloth, activate irrigation frost protection, delay spray application, evacuate field workers, or secure equipment. Sourced from FMIS decision support rules or NWS/DTN advisory guidance.
attributes.references: GLOBALG.A.P. Good Agricultural Practices (GAP); USDA Best Management Practices (BMP); EPA Restricted Entry Interval (REI) Compliance; OSHA Worker Safety Standards

attributes.name: relative_humidity_pct
attributes.description: Forecast or observed relative humidity percentage at the time of alert issuance. Used in frost risk assessment (high humidity increases frost severity), spray window determination, and disease pressure prediction for Integrated Pest Management (IPM).

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: Severity tier of the weather alert following NWS standard classification. Advisory indicates conditions that may cause inconvenience; Watch indicates conditions are favorable for a hazard; Warning indicates a hazard is imminent or occurring; Emergency indicates an extreme, life-threatening event.

attributes.name: spray_window_open
attributes.description: Indicates whether pesticide or fertilizer spray application is permissible during the alert period based on wind speed, temperature, humidity, and precipitation conditions. False indicates spray operations should be suspended per EPA application restrictions and Good Agricultural Practices (GAP).

attributes.name: start_timestamp
attributes.description: The datetime when the hazardous weather conditions described in the alert are expected to begin or have begun. Used for scheduling protective actions such as frost cloth deployment, irrigation frost protection activation, and spray window closure.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

attributes.name: wind_speed_ms
attributes.description: Forecast or observed wind speed in metres per second at the time of alert issuance. Relevant for high wind alerts, spray window assessment, frost risk modification (wind reduces radiation frost risk), and wildfire smoke dispersion modeling.
